title.zh: 卷一百四十五 列傳第九十五: 劉玄佐 董晉 陸長源 劉全諒 李忠臣 李希烈 吳少誠
title.en: Volume 145 Biographies 95: Liu Xuanzuo, Dong Jin, Lu Zhengyuan, Liu Quanliang, Li Zhongchen, Li Xilie, Wu Shaocheng
title.raw: 卷一百四十五 列傳第九十五: 劉玄佐 董晉 陸長源 劉全諒 李忠臣 李希烈 吳少誠 Volume 145 Biographies 95: Liu Xuanzuo, Dong Jin, Lu Zhengyuan, Liu Quanliang, Li Zhongchen, Li Xilie, Wu Shaocheng

sentences.zh: 劉玄佐，本名洽，滑州匡城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Xuanzuo, original name Qia, was a native of Kuangcheng in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuanzuo, whose original name was Qia, came from Kuangcheng in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻，不理生業；

translations.literal: In youth he was dashing and unconstrained and did not attend to making a living;
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was bold and free-spirited and paid no heed to earning a livelihood;

sentences.zh: 為縣捕盜吏，違法，為令所笞，僅死，乃亡命從軍。

translations.literal: He served as a county officer catching thieves, violated the law, was flogged by the magistrate nearly to death, and then fled as an outlaw to join the army.
translations.idiomatic: He became a county constable hunting thieves, broke the law, was beaten by the magistrate almost to death, and finally fled as a fugitive to enlist.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，為永平軍衙將。

translations.literal: In the Dali era he became a yajiang of the Yongping army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali period he served as a staff commander in the Yongping army.

sentences.zh: 李靈曜據汴州，洽將兵乘其無備，徑入宋州，遂詔以州隸永平軍，節度使李勉奏署宋州刺史。

translations.literal: When Li Lingyao held Bian Prefecture, Qia led troops and, seizing his unpreparedness, went straight into Song Prefecture; the court then ordered that the prefecture be attached to the Yongping army, and the military governor Li Mian memorialized to appoint him Song prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Lingyao seized Bian Prefecture, Qia led troops in while the enemy was off guard and marched straight into Song Prefecture. The court then placed the prefecture under the Yongping army, and Military Governor Li Mian memorialized to appoint him prefect of Song.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，加兼御史中丞、亳潁節度等使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong he was additionally made concurrent Censor-in-chief and Bao-Ying circuit commissioner, among other posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jianzhong reign he was further appointed concurrent Censor-in-chief and commissioner of the Bo-Ying circuit, among other duties.

sentences.zh: 李正己死，子納匿喪謀叛，而李洧以徐州歸順，納遣兵圍之。

translations.literal: Li Zhengji died; his son Na concealed the death and plotted rebellion; Li Wei surrendered Xuzhou to the court, and Na sent troops to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zhengji died, his son Na concealed the death and plotted rebellion, while Li Wei surrendered Xuzhou to the throne. Na then sent troops to besiege him.

sentences.zh: 詔洽與諸軍援洧，與賊接戰，大破之，斬首萬余級。

translations.literal: The court ordered Qia and the various armies to aid Wei; joining battle with the rebels, they utterly defeated them and beheaded more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Qia and the allied armies to relieve Wei. In battle with the rebels they won a great victory and took more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 由是轉輸路通，加御史大夫。

translations.literal: Thereby the transport routes were opened, and he was promoted to Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: With the supply routes restored, he was promoted to Grand Censor.

sentences.zh: 又收濮州，降其將楊令暉，分兵挾之，徇濮陽，降其將高彥昭，以通濮陽津。

translations.literal: He also took Pu Prefecture, inducing its general Yang Linghui to submit; dividing troops to flank him, he marched on Puyang and induced its general Gao Yanzhao to submit, thereby opening the Puyang crossing.
translations.idiomatic: He also recovered Pu Prefecture and won the submission of its general Yang Linghui. Sending detachments to support the advance, he pushed on to Puyang and won over its general Gao Yanzhao, opening the crossing at Puyang.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書，累封四百戶，兼曹濮觀察使，尋加淄青兗鄆招討使，又加汴滑都統副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister, enfeoffed cumulatively with four hundred households, made concurrent Ca-Pu observation commissioner, soon added as Zi-Qing-Yan-Yan pacification commissioner, and again made deputy overall commander of Bian-Hua.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister, his fief was increased by four hundred households, he was made concurrent Ca-Pu observation commissioner, soon afterward added as pacification commissioner for Zi, Qing, Yan, and Yan circuits, and later made deputy overall commander of Bian and Hua.

sentences.zh: 李希烈攻汴州，德宗在奉天，連戰，賊稍卻。

translations.literal: Li Xilie attacked Bian Prefecture; Dezong was at Fengtian; after repeated battles the rebels gradually retreated.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie attacked Bian Prefecture, Emperor Dezong was at Fengtian. After a series of engagements the rebels gradually fell back.

sentences.zh: 興元初，進加檢校左僕射，加平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xingyuan he was advanced to acting Left Vice Director and given the title of Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Xingyuan era he was promoted to acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and made Associate Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 希烈圍寧陵，洽大將劉昌言堅守不下。

translations.literal: Xilie besieged Ningling; Qia's great general Liu Changyan held firm and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: When Xilie besieged Ningling, Qia's chief general Liu Changyan held the city and refused to surrender.

sentences.zh: 希烈攻陳州，洽遣昌言與諸軍救之，大敗賊黨，獲其將翟崇暉。

translations.literal: Xilie attacked Chen Prefecture; Qia sent Changyan with the various armies to rescue it, utterly defeating the rebel band and capturing their general Zhai Chonghui.
translations.idiomatic: When Xilie attacked Chen Prefecture, Qia sent Changyan with the allied armies to relieve the city. They routed the rebels and captured the enemy general Zhai Chonghui.

sentences.zh: 希烈棄汴州，洽率軍收汴，詔加汴宋節度。

translations.literal: Xilie abandoned Bian Prefecture; Qia led the army to recover Bian; the court ordered him added as Bian-Song military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie abandoned Bian Prefecture, and Qia led his army to recover it. The court then appointed him military governor of Bian and Song.

sentences.zh: 無幾，授本管及陳州諸軍行營都統，賜名玄佐。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed overall commander of his own circuit and the various armies of Chen Prefecture, and granted the name Xuanzuo.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made overall commander of his own command and of the Chen Prefecture field armies, and was granted the name Xuanzuo.

sentences.zh: 是歲來朝，又拜涇原四鎮北庭等道兵馬副元帥，檢校司空，益封八百戶。

translations.literal: That year he came to court; he was again appointed vice marshal of Jingyuan, the Four Garrisons, Beiting and other routes, acting Minister of Works, with an additional enfeoffment of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: That year he came to court and was further appointed vice commander-in-chief of the armies of Jingyuan, the Four Garrisons, Beiting, and other circuits, acting Minister of Works, with his fief increased by eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 玄佐性豪侈，輕財重義，厚賞軍士，故百姓益困。

translations.literal: Xuanzuo's nature was extravagant and ostentatious; he treated wealth lightly and valued righteousness, richly rewarded the soldiers, so the common people grew ever more distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzuo was lavish by nature, careless of wealth but mindful of loyalty, and he rewarded his troops generously—so the common people grew ever poorer.

sentences.zh: 是以汴之卒，始於李忠臣，訖於玄佐，而日益驕恣，多逐殺將帥，以利剽劫。

translations.literal: Thus the troops of Bian, from Li Zhongchen down to Xuanzuo, daily grew more arrogant and unrestrained, often driving out and killing commanders for the sake of plunder.
translations.idiomatic: From Li Zhongchen down to Xuanzuo, the soldiers of Bian grew daily more arrogant and violent, often deposing and killing their commanders so they could loot at will.

sentences.zh: 又寵任小吏張士南及養子樂士朝，財物鉅萬。

translations.literal: He also favored and employed the petty clerk Zhang Shinan and his adopted son Yue Shichao, whose wealth reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He also lavished favor on the minor clerk Zhang Shinan and on his adopted son Yue Shichao, who amassed wealth in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 士朝通玄佐嬖妾。

translations.literal: Shichao had relations with Xuanzuo's favorite concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Shichao carried on an affair with Xuanzuo's favorite concubine.

sentences.zh: 玄佐在鎮，李納每使來，必重贈遺，飾美女名樂，從其遊娛，故多得其陰事，常先為備，故納憚其心計。

translations.literal: While Xuanzuo was in his post, whenever Li Na sent envoys, he always gave them rich gifts, adorned beautiful women and famous musicians for their entertainment, and thus often learned their secret affairs, always preparing in advance, so Na feared his schemes.
translations.idiomatic: While Xuanzuo held his post, whenever Li Na sent envoys he showered them with rich gifts, furnished them with beautiful women and skilled musicians for their diversion, and thus often learned their secrets in advance. Na came to fear his cunning.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年三月，薨於位，年五十八，廢朝三日，贈太傅。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Zhenyuan he died in office at age fifty-eight; court was suspended three days; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year of Zhenyuan he died in office at the age of fifty-eight. Court audiences were suspended for three days, and he was posthumously ennobled as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 將佐初匿喪，稱疾俟代，帝亦為隱，數日乃發喪。

translations.literal: His officers at first concealed the death, claiming illness while awaiting a replacement; the emperor also concealed it; only after several days was the death announced.
translations.idiomatic: At first his staff concealed the death, claiming he was ill and awaiting a successor; the emperor colluded in the concealment, and the mourning was not announced until several days had passed.

sentences.zh: 子士寧、士幹。

translations.literal: His sons were Shining and Shigan.
translations.idiomatic: He had sons named Shining and Shigan.

sentences.zh: 初，將佐匿喪，既發，帝遣問所欲立：「吳湊可乎？」

translations.literal: At first, when the officers concealed the death—after it was announced—the emperor sent to ask whom they wished to install: "Would Wu Cou do?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the staff had concealed the death and the mourning was finally announced, the emperor sent to ask whom they wished to install: "Would Wu Cou be acceptable?"

sentences.zh: 監軍孟介、行軍盧瑗皆曰「便」。

translations.literal: The army supervisor Meng Jie and the army commander Lu Yuan both said "suitable."
translations.idiomatic: Army Supervisor Meng Jie and Army Commander Lu Yuan both replied, "Suitable."

sentences.zh: 及湊次汜水，柩將遷，請備儀；

translations.literal: When Cou reached Sishui, as the coffin was about to be moved, he requested funeral escort;
translations.idiomatic: When Cou reached Sishui and the coffin was about to be moved on, he requested a proper funeral escort;

sentences.zh: 瑗不許，又令留什物俟新使，將士大怒。

translations.literal: Yuan would not permit it, and also ordered that belongings be held for the new envoy; officers and soldiers were greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan refused and also ordered that the deceased's belongings be held for the incoming commissioner. Officers and soldiers were furious.

sentences.zh: 玄佐子婿及親兵乃以三月晦夜激怒三軍。

translations.literal: Xuanzuo's sons-in-law and personal guard then on the last night of the third month incited the three armies.
translations.idiomatic: On the last night of the third month, Xuanzuo's sons-in-law and personal troops incited the entire army.

sentences.zh: 明晨，衙兵皆甲胄，擁士寧登重榻，衣以墨缞，呼為留後。

translations.literal: At dawn the guard soldiers all wore armor, supported Shining onto a raised couch, clothed him in black mourning dress, and hailed him as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the guard troops all donned armor, lifted Shining onto a high couch, dressed him in black mourning garb, and proclaimed him acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 軍士執城將曹金岸、浚儀令李邁，曰：「爾等皆請吳湊者！」

translations.literal: The soldiers seized the city general Cao Jin'an and Junyi magistrate Li Mai, saying: "You are the ones who asked for Wu Cou!"
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers seized City General Cao Jin'an and Junyi Magistrate Li Mai, crying: "You were the ones who wanted Wu Cou!"

sentences.zh: 遂臠之，唯盧瑗獲免。

translations.literal: They then dismembered them; only Lu Yuan was spared.
translations.idiomatic: They then hacked them to pieces. Only Lu Yuan was spared.

sentences.zh: 士寧乃以財物分賜將士，請之為帥，孟介以聞。

translations.literal: Shining then distributed property to reward the officers and soldiers, requested to be made commander; Meng Jie reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Shining distributed goods to reward the troops and asked to be made commander. Meng Jie reported this to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝召宰臣問計，竇參曰：「今汴人挾李納以邀命，若不許，懼合於納。」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the chief ministers to ask counsel; Dou Can said: "Now the men of Bian hold Li Na hostage to demand appointment; if we do not grant it, we fear they will join Na."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned his chief ministers for counsel. Dou Can said: "The men of Bian are using Li Na as leverage to demand an appointment. If we refuse, I fear they will join Na."

sentences.zh: 遂從之，授士寧起復金吾衛將軍同正、汴州刺史、宣武軍節度等使。

translations.literal: He assented, appointing Shining on mourning leave restored as General of the Golden Guards with concurrent status, Bian prefect, Bian military commissioner, etc.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and appointed Shining, restored from mourning, as General of the Golden Guards with concurrent status, prefect of Bian, and military governor of the Xuanwu army, among other titles.

sentences.zh: 士寧位未定時，遣使通王武俊、劉濟、田緒，以士寧未受詔於國，皆留之。

translations.literal: While Shining's position was not yet settled, he sent envoys to Wang Wujun, Liu Ji, and Tian Xu; because Shining had not yet received imperial commission, all detained them.
translations.idiomatic: While Shining's appointment was still unsettled, he sent envoys to Wang Wujun, Liu Ji, and Tian Xu, but because he had not yet received an imperial commission, all three detained his messengers.

sentences.zh: 士寧初授節制，諸將多不悅服。

translations.literal: When Shining was first granted the military commission, many generals were displeased and unwilling to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Shining first received his commission, many of his generals were discontent and refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 性忍暴淫亂，或彎弓挺刃，手殺人於杯案間，悉烝父之妓妾，又強取人之婦女，好倮觀婦人。

translations.literal: His nature was cruel, violent, and debauched; sometimes bending bow and drawing blade he killed people at the wine table; he took all his father's singing girls and concubines, also forcibly seized others' wives and daughters, and liked to watch women naked.
translations.idiomatic: He was cruel, violent, and debauched. Sometimes he would bend his bow or draw his blade and kill men at the banquet table. He took all his father's entertainers and concubines for himself, forcibly seized other men's wives and daughters, and liked to watch women unclothed.

sentences.zh: 每出畋獵，數日方還，軍府苦之。

translations.literal: Whenever he went out hunting, he would not return for several days; the military headquarters suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went hunting he would be away for days on end, to the great distress of the headquarters.

sentences.zh: 其大將李萬榮與其父玄佐同里闬，少相善，寬厚得眾心；

translations.literal: His great general Li Wanrong was from the same village as his father Xuanzuo; they had been on good terms since youth; he was generous and won the hearts of the masses;
translations.idiomatic: His chief general Li Wanrong came from the same village as his father Xuanzuo; they had been close since youth, and Wanrong was generous and won the troops' loyalty;

sentences.zh: 士寧疑之，去其兵權，令攝汴州事。

translations.literal: Shining was suspicious of him, removed his military authority, and ordered him to act as Bian prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Shining grew suspicious of him, stripped him of military command, and ordered him to administer Bian Prefecture in an acting capacity.

sentences.zh: 萬榮深怨之，將伺其隙逐之。

translations.literal: Wanrong deeply resented this and planned to seize an opportunity to drive him out.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong deeply resented this and bided his time to drive Shining out.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，士寧以眾二萬畋於城南，兵既出，萬榮晨入士寧廨舍，召其所留心腹兵千余人，矯謂之曰：「有詔征大夫入朝，俾吾掌留務，汝輩人賜錢三千貫，無他憂也。」

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year, Shining with twenty thousand men hunted south of the city; once the troops had gone out, Wanrong early in the morning entered Shining's office, summoned more than a thousand trusted core troops he had cultivated, and falsely told them: "There is an edict summoning the envoy to court, making me handle the acting post; each of you will be given three thousand strings of cash—no other worries."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth year Shining took twenty thousand men hunting south of the city. Once the army had marched out, Wanrong entered Shining's headquarters at dawn, summoned more than a thousand trusted troops he had cultivated, and falsely announced: "An edict summons the commissioner to court and appoints me to handle affairs in his stead. Each of you will receive three thousand strings of cash—have no other concern."

sentences.zh: 兵士皆拜。

translations.literal: The soldiers all bowed.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers all bowed in assent.

sentences.zh: 萬榮既約親兵於內，又召各營兵於外，以是言令之，軍士皆聽命。

translations.literal: Wanrong having arranged with the personal guard within, also summoned the troops of each camp outside and gave them this order; all obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Having secured the personal guard within, Wanrong also summoned the troops of every camp outside and gave them the same order. The whole army obeyed.

sentences.zh: 萬榮乃分兵閉城門，馳使白士寧曰：「詔征大夫，宜速即路；

translations.literal: Wanrong then divided troops to shut the city gates and sent a fast messenger to tell Shining: "An edict summons the envoy—you should hurry on your way;
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong then posted troops to close the city gates and sent a fast rider to tell Shining: "An edict summons you to court. You should set out at once;

sentences.zh: 若遷延不行，當傳首以獻。」

translations.literal: if you delay and do not go, your head will be sent in tribute."
translations.idiomatic: if you linger, your head will be sent to the capital instead."

sentences.zh: 士寧知眾不為用，計無所出，乃將五百騎走歸京師。

translations.literal: Shining knew the masses would not serve him, had no plan, and fled to the capital with five hundred cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Shining saw that the army would not follow him and could think of no recourse. He fled to the capital with five hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 比至中牟，亡走大半；

translations.literal: By the time he reached Zhongmou, more than half had fled;
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Zhongmou, more than half his followers had deserted;

sentences.zh: 至東都，所余僮隸婢妾數十人而已。

translations.literal: when he reached the eastern capital, only a few dozen servants and concubines remained.
translations.idiomatic: and when he reached the eastern capital only a few dozen servants and concubines were left.

sentences.zh: 既至京師，詔令歸第服喪，禁絕出入。

translations.literal: Having reached the capital, he was ordered to return to his residence to observe mourning and was forbidden to go in or out.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the capital he was ordered to return home to observe mourning and was forbidden to leave his residence.

sentences.zh: 萬榮乃斬士寧所親之將辛液、白英賢以令於軍，凡賞軍士錢二十萬貫，詔令籍沒士寧家財以分賞焉。

translations.literal: Wanrong then beheaded Shining's close generals Xin Ye and Bai Yingxian to command the army; in all he rewarded the soldiers two hundred thousand strings; the court ordered Shining's family property confiscated and distributed as rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong then executed Shining's favored generals Xin Ye and Bai Yingxian to assert control over the army. He distributed two hundred thousand strings of cash to reward the troops, and the court ordered Shining's family property confiscated and divided among them.

sentences.zh: 遂授萬榮宣武軍兵馬留後。

translations.literal: Wanrong was then appointed acting military commissioner of the Xuanwu army.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong was then appointed acting military commissioner of the Xuanwu army.

sentences.zh: 初，萬榮遣兵三千備秋於京西，有親兵三百，前為劉士寧所驕者，日益橫。

translations.literal: At first Wanrong had sent three thousand troops to garrison autumn defense in western Jing; there were three hundred personal guards who had previously been indulged by Liu Shining, growing daily more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wanrong had sent three thousand troops to garrison the autumn defenses west of the capital. Among them were three hundred personal guards whom Liu Shining had long indulged, and they grew daily more insolent.

sentences.zh: 萬榮惡之，悉置行籍中，由是深怨萬榮。

translations.literal: Wanrong hated them and put them all on the campaign roster; thereby they deeply resented Wanrong.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong disliked them and placed them all on the active campaign rolls, for which they came to hate him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 大將韓惟清、張彥琳請將往，不許；

translations.literal: The great generals Han Weiqing and Zhang Yanlin requested to lead them; permission was denied;
translations.idiomatic: Generals Han Weiqing and Zhang Yanlin asked to lead the detachment, but Wanrong refused;

sentences.zh: 萬榮令其子乃將之，未發。

translations.literal: Wanrong ordered his son Nai to lead them; they had not yet departed.
translations.idiomatic: he ordered his son Nai to command them instead, but the column had not yet set out.

sentences.zh: 惟清、彥琳不得誌，因親兵銜怨，乃作亂，共攻萬榮。

translations.literal: Weiqing and Yanlin did not get their wish; relying on the personal guards' grievance, they raised rebellion and jointly attacked Wanrong.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqing and Yanlin, thwarted in their request, joined with the resentful personal guard to mutiny and attack Wanrong together.

sentences.zh: 萬榮分兵擊之，叛卒兵械少，戰不勝，乃劫轉運財貨及居人而潰，殺傷千余人。

translations.literal: Wanrong divided troops to attack them; the rebels had few arms, could not win in battle, then plundered transport goods and residents and dispersed, killing and wounding more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong sent troops against them. The mutineers were poorly armed, could not prevail, then looted transport stores and civilians and broke apart, killing and wounding more than a thousand people.

sentences.zh: 叛兵四出，多投宋州，刺史劉逸準厚撫之。

translations.literal: The rebel soldiers scattered in all directions, many going to Song Prefecture; the prefect Liu Yizhun treated them generously.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels scattered in all directions, many fleeing to Song Prefecture, where Prefect Liu Yizhun treated them generously.

sentences.zh: 韓惟清走鄭州，張彥琳走東都，以束身歸罪，宥以不死，並流竄焉。

translations.literal: Han Weiqing fled to Zheng Prefecture, Zhang Yanlin fled to the eastern capital; binding themselves to surrender, they were spared death and both were banished.
translations.idiomatic: Han Weiqing fled to Zheng Prefecture and Zhang Yanlin to the eastern capital. Both surrendered to accept punishment, were spared execution, and were banished.

sentences.zh: 萬榮悉捕逃叛將卒妻孥數千人，皆誅之。

translations.literal: Wanrong captured all the wives and children of the fugitive rebel officers and soldiers—several thousand—and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong seized the wives and children of the fugitive mutineers—several thousand in all—and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 萬榮誅叛卒之後，人心恟々不安，軍卒數人呼於市曰：「今夜大兵四面至，城當破。」

translations.literal: After Wanrong executed the rebels, people's hearts were restless and uneasy; several soldiers cried in the market: "Tonight great armies will arrive from all four sides—the city will fall."
translations.idiomatic: After executing the mutineers, Wanrong left the city uneasy. Several soldiers shouted in the market: "Tonight great armies will come from every side and the city will fall."

sentences.zh: 眾驚駭。

translations.literal: The masses were terrified.
translations.idiomatic: The populace panicked.

sentences.zh: 萬榮悉捕得，或云士寧所教，萬榮斬之以聞；

translations.literal: Wanrong captured them all; some said Shining had instigated it; Wanrong beheaded them and reported;
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong seized them all. Some said Shining had instigated the alarm; Wanrong executed them and reported to the court;

sentences.zh: 遂以士寧廢處郴州。

translations.literal: Shining was then deposed and sent to Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: and Shining was deposed and banished to Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十一年五月，授萬榮宣武軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eleventh year, Wanrong was appointed military governor of the Xuanwu army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eleventh year Wanrong was appointed full military governor of the Xuanwu army.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，萬榮病，遂署其子乃為司馬。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year Wanrong fell ill and appointed his son Nai as deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, in the eighth month, Wanrong fell ill and appointed his son Nai deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 乃勒大將李湛、伊婁涚、張伾往外鎮，尋皆令殺之。

translations.literal: Nai compelled the great generals Li Zhan, Yi Louce, and Zhang Pi to go to outer posts, then soon ordered them all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Nai forced the senior generals Li Zhan, Yi Louce, and Zhang Pi to take posts in outlying garrisons, then soon ordered them all killed.

sentences.zh: 涚、伾皆已死，惟李湛至尉氏，尉氏鎮將郝忠節不肯殺湛。

translations.literal: Louce and Pi were already dead; only Li Zhan reached Weishi; the Weishi garrison commander Hao Zhongjie refused to kill Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Louce and Pi were already dead. Li Zhan alone reached Weishi, where Garrison Commander Hao Zhongjie refused to kill him.

sentences.zh: 是夜軍士逐出李乃，遂執送京師。

translations.literal: That night the soldiers expelled Li Nai and escorted him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That night the troops drove out Li Nai and sent him under guard to the capital.

sentences.zh: 萬榮以其日病卒。

translations.literal: Wanrong died of illness the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong died of his illness that same day.

sentences.zh: 乃至京師，付京兆府杖殺。

translations.literal: When Nai reached the capital, he was handed to the Jingzhao prefecture and beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Nai reached the capital he was handed over to the metropolitan prefecture and beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 劉士幹，玄佐養子，前為太府少卿。

translations.literal: Liu Shigan, Xuanzuo's adopted son, had previously been Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shigan, an adopted son of Xuanzuo, had formerly served as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 有樂士朝者，亦為玄佐養子，因冒劉姓，與士幹有隙。

translations.literal: There was one Yue Shichao, also Xuanzuo's adopted son, who had falsely taken the Liu surname and had a rift with Shigan.
translations.idiomatic: Another adopted son, Yue Shichao, had falsely taken the surname Liu and was at odds with Shigan.

sentences.zh: 及玄佐卒，或云為士朝所鴆。

translations.literal: When Xuanzuo died, some said he had been poisoned by Shichao.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzuo died, some said Shichao had poisoned him.

sentences.zh: 士幹知之，及至京師，遣奴持刀於喪位，語士朝曰：「有吊客至。」

translations.literal: Shigan knew it; when he reached the capital he sent a slave with a blade at the mourning site and told Shichao: "Mourning guests have come."
translations.idiomatic: Shigan believed this. When he reached the capital he sent a slave with a blade to the mourning hall and told Shichao, "Mourners have arrived."

sentences.zh: 因誘殺之。

translations.literal: He then lured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He then lured Shichao out and killed him.

sentences.zh: 賜士幹死。

translations.literal: Shigan was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shigan was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 董晉，字混成，河中盧鄉人。

translations.literal: Dong Jin, courtesy name Huncheng, was a native of Luxiang in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jin, courtesy name Huncheng, came from Luxiang in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 明經及第。

translations.literal: He passed the classics examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Metropolitan Examination in the Classics.

sentences.zh: 至德初，肅宗自靈武幸彭原，晉上書謁見，授校書郎、翰林待制，再轉衛尉丞，出為汾州司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide, when Suzong went from Lingwu to Pengyuan, Jin presented a memorial and was received, appointed Proofreader and Hanlin attendant, then transferred twice to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Studs, and sent out as Fenzhou Vice Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhide, when Emperor Suzong traveled from Lingwu to Pengyuan, Jin submitted a memorial and was received in audience. He was appointed Proofreader and Hanlin attendant, later promoted twice to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and then sent out as vice prefect of Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，刺史崔圓改淮南節度，奏晉以本官攝殿中侍御史，充判官，尋歸臺，授本官，遷侍御史、主客員外郎、祠部郎中。

translations.literal: Before long the prefect Cui Yuan was transferred to Huainan military governor; he memorialized for Jin to act as Palace Attendant censor with his original rank, serving as administrative aide; soon he returned to the censorate, received his original post, and was promoted to Attending Censor, Supernumerary Director of Reception, and Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Prefect Cui Yuan was transferred to military governor of Huainan and memorialized for Jin to serve as acting Palace Attendant censor at his former rank and as administrative aide. Soon Jin returned to the censorate, received his former title, and was promoted to Attending Censor, Supernumerary Director of the Bureau of Reception, and Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，兵部侍郎李涵送崇徽公主使回紇，奏晉為判官。

translations.literal: In the Dali era, Vice Minister of War Li Han escorted Princess Chonghui to the Uyghurs; he memorialized for Jin as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali era Vice Minister of War Li Han escorted Princess Chonghui on a mission to the Uyghurs and memorialized for Jin to serve as his administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 使還，拜司勛郎中。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, he was appointed Director of the Bureau of Merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the embassy returned, Jin was appointed Director of the Bureau of Merit.

sentences.zh: 歷秘書太府太常少卿監、左金吾將軍。

translations.literal: He successively served as Supervisor of the Secretariat, Court of Imperial Treasury, and Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and General of the Left Golden Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Supervisor of the Secretariat, of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, and of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and as General of the Left Golden Guards.

sentences.zh: 旬日，德宗嗣位，改太常卿，遷右散騎常侍，兼御史中丞知臺事。

translations.literal: Within ten days Dezong succeeded to the throne; he was changed to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, promoted to Right Regular Attendant, and made concurrent Censor-in-chief directing censorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days Emperor Dezong succeeded to the throne. Jin was made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, promoted to Right Regular Attendant, and appointed concurrent Censor-in-chief in charge of censorate affairs.

sentences.zh: 以清勤謹慎，故驟遷右職。

translations.literal: Because of his purity, diligence, and prudence, he was rapidly promoted to high office on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was pure, diligent, and careful, he rose rapidly to high office.

sentences.zh: 尋為華州刺史、兼御史中丞、潼關防禦使。

translations.literal: Soon he became Hua prefect, concurrent Censor-in-chief, and Tong Pass defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became prefect of Hua, concurrent Censor-in-chief, and defense commissioner of Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 久之，加兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: After a long while he was additionally made concurrent Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was further made concurrent Grand Censor.

sentences.zh: 硃泚僭逆於京師，使兇黨仇敬、何望之侵逼華州，晉奔遁赴行在，授國子祭酒，尋令往恆州宣慰。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci usurped in the capital and sent his villainous followers Qiu Jing and He Wangzhi to invade Hua Prefecture; Jin fled to the imperial camp, was appointed Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, and soon ordered to go to Hengzhou to offer consolation.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled in the capital he sent his henchmen Qiu Jing and He Wangzhi to threaten Hua Prefecture. Jin fled to the imperial camp, was appointed Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, and soon after was sent to Hengzhou to offer consolation.

sentences.zh: 從車駕還京師，遷左金吾衛大將軍，改尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Following the imperial carriage back to the capital, he was transferred to Grand General of the Left Golden Guards and changed to Left Vice Director of the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the imperial carriage back to the capital and was transferred to Grand General of the Left Golden Guards, then made Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 時右丞元琇領度支使，為韓滉所擠貶黜，晉嫉之，見宰相極言非罪，舉朝稱之。

translations.literal: At that time the Right Vice Director Yuan Xiu headed the fiscal commission and was squeezed out and demoted by Han Huang; Jin resented this, saw the chancellor and strongly declared his innocence; the whole court praised him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Right Vice Director Yuan Xiu headed the fiscal commission and was forced out and demoted by Han Huang. Jin took offense at this, went to the chancellor, and forcefully argued Yuan's innocence. The whole court praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 復拜太常卿。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Chancellery and made Associate Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 時政事決在竇參，晉但奉詔書，領然諾而已。

translations.literal: At that time government decisions rested with Dou Can; Jin only received edicts and gave assent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time policy rested with Dou Can; Jin merely received edicts and gave his assent.

sentences.zh: 金吾衛將軍沈房有弟喪，公除，衣慘服入閣。

translations.literal: Golden Guards General Shen Fang had a brother's death; after public mourning ended, he wore pale mourning dress into the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: Golden Guards General Shen Fang had lost a brother. When the period of public mourning ended, he entered the Inner Court wearing pale mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 上問宰相，對曰：「準式，朝官有周年已下喪者，諸騑縵，不合衣淺色。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked the chancellor, who replied: "According to regulation, when court officials have mourning under one year, all use piebald and gray—wearing light colors is improper."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the chancellor, who replied: "By regulation, when a court official is in mourning for less than a full year, all should wear dappled or gray mourning dress. Light-colored garments are not proper."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「南班安得有之？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How could the southern ranks have such a thing?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "How could the southern ranks have such a practice?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「因循而然。」

translations.literal: He replied: "It came about through mere custom."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "It is simply force of habit."

sentences.zh: 又問晉冠冕之制，對曰：「古人服冠冕者，動有佩玉之響，所以節步也。

translations.literal: He also asked Jin about the system of caps and robes, and Jin replied: "When the ancients wore caps and robes, their movements were accompanied by the sound of pendant jades, by which they regulated their steps.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also asked about court dress. Jin replied, "When the ancients wore caps and robes, the jade pendants at their belts chimed as they walked, regulating their pace.

sentences.zh: 《禮》雲『堂上接武，堂下布武』，至恭也；

translations.literal: The Rites say, 'On the hall above, steps touch one after another; below the hall, steps are spread wide'—this is the height of reverence;
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say, 'On the hall floor the steps nearly overlap; below the hall they are spread wide'—the utmost in reverence;

sentences.zh: 步武有常，君前之禮，進趨而已。

translations.literal: the pace has a fixed measure; before the ruler the ritual is only to advance with quickened steps.
translations.idiomatic: a measured gait is prescribed, and before the sovereign one need only quicken one's pace.

sentences.zh: 今或奔走以致顛仆，非恭慎也。

translations.literal: Now some run and thereby fall—this is not reverent caution.
translations.idiomatic: Today men run and stumble—this is not reverent caution.

sentences.zh: 在式，朝官皆是綾袍袱，五品已上金玉帶，取其文彩畫飭，以奉上也。

translations.literal: By regulation, court officials all wear damask robes with overlapping collars; those of the fifth rank and above wear belts of gold and jade, taking patterned ornament to adorn themselves in service of the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: By regulation court officials wear damask robes with overlapping collars; from the fifth rank upward they wear gold and jade belts, their patterned dress serving to honor the throne.

sentences.zh: 是以禹惡衣食而致美乎黻冕，君親一致。

translations.literal: Thus Yu disdained mere clothing and food yet made his patterned caps and robes beautiful; ruler and subject are alike in this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yu scorned plain dress yet made his ceremonial caps and robes splendid—sovereign and subject alike in this principle.

sentences.zh: 昔尚書郎含香，老萊彩服，皆此義也。

translations.literal: In former times Attending Gentlemen of the Masters of Writing carried incense, and Laolai wore colored garments for his parents—both embody this meaning.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Masters of Writing carried incense at court, and Laolai wore bright garments for his parents—both express the same idea.

sentences.zh: 服絁縵，非制也。」

translations.literal: Wearing coarse silk mourning is not according to regulation."
translations.idiomatic: Wearing plain silk mourning dress is not proper."

sentences.zh: 上深然之，遂詔曰：「常參官入閣，不得趨走；

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved and thereupon issued an edict: "Regular attending officials entering the Inner Court must not run;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor strongly agreed and issued an edict: "Regular attending officials entering the Inner Court must not run;

sentences.zh: 周期已下喪者，禁慘服朝會。」

translations.literal: those in mourning for less than a full year are forbidden pale mourning dress at court assemblies."
translations.idiomatic: those in mourning for less than a full year are forbidden to attend court in pale mourning dress."

sentences.zh: 又令服本品綾袍金玉帶。

translations.literal: He also ordered them to wear their rank's damask robes and gold-jade belts.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered them to wear their proper rank's damask robes and gold-jade belts.

sentences.zh: 晉明於禮學如此。

translations.literal: Jin was thus clear in ritual learning.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was this well versed in ritual learning.

sentences.zh: 竇參驕滿既甚，帝漸惡之。

translations.literal: Dou Can had grown extremely arrogant and overbearing, and the emperor gradually came to dislike him.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Can had grown insufferably arrogant, and the emperor came to dislike him.

sentences.zh: 八年，參諷晉奏其侄給事中竇申為吏部侍郎，帝正色曰：「豈不是竇參遣卿奏也？」

translations.literal: In the eighth year Can induced Jin to memorialize that his nephew, Attending Gentleman Dou Shen, be made Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel; the emperor said sternly: "Was this not Dou Can who sent you to memorialize?"
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Can had Jin memorialize appointing his nephew Attending Gentleman Dou Shen Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel. The emperor said sternly, "Did Dou Can not send you to submit this?"

sentences.zh: 晉不敢隱。

translations.literal: Jin did not dare conceal it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin did not dare hide the truth.

sentences.zh: 因問參過失，晉具奏之。

translations.literal: The emperor then asked about Can's faults, and Jin reported them all in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked about Can's misconduct, and Jin reported it in full.

sentences.zh: 旬日，參貶官，晉憂懼，累上表辭位。

translations.literal: Within ten days Can was demoted; Jin was fearful and repeatedly submitted memorials resigning his post.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days Can was demoted. Jin was alarmed and repeatedly asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 九年夏，改禮部尚書、兵部尚書、東都留守、東都畿汝州都防禦使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, summer, he was changed to Minister of Rites, Minister of War, eastern capital regent, and overall defense commissioner of the eastern capital circuit and Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the ninth year he was made Minister of Rites, Minister of War, regent of the eastern capital, and overall defense commissioner of the eastern capital circuit and Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會汴州節度李萬榮疾甚，其子乃為亂，以晉為檢校左僕射、同平章事，兼汴州刺史、宣武軍節度營田、汴宋觀察使。

translations.literal: When Bian Prefecture Military Governor Li Wanrong fell gravely ill and his son Nai raised a disturbance, Jin was appointed acting Left Vice Director, Associate Grand Councilor, concurrent Bian prefect, and military governor of the Xuanwu army with charge of garrison fields and Bian-Song observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Military Governor Li Wanrong of Bian Prefecture fell gravely ill and his son Nai mutinied, Jin was appointed acting Left Vice Director, Associate Grand Councilor, concurrent prefect of Bian, and military governor of the Xuanwu army with charge of garrison fields and Bian-Song observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 晉既受命，唯將幕官傔從等十數人，都不召集兵馬。

translations.literal: Once Jin received the appointment, he took only a dozen or so staff officers and attendants and did not summon troops at all.
translations.idiomatic: On receiving his commission Jin took only a dozen or so staff officers and attendants and did not raise troops at all.

sentences.zh: 既至鄭州，宣武軍迎候將吏無至者。

translations.literal: When he reached Zheng Prefecture, not a single welcoming officer of the Xuanwu army came to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Zheng Prefecture, not one welcoming officer from the Xuanwu army appeared.

sentences.zh: 晉左右及鄭州官吏皆懼，共勸晉云：「鄧惟恭承萬榮疾病之甚，遂總領軍州事。

translations.literal: Jin's attendants and the Zheng Prefecture officials were all afraid and jointly urged Jin, saying: "Deng Weigong, taking advantage of Wanrong's grave illness, has already assumed overall control of the army and prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's attendants and the officials of Zheng Prefecture were terrified and urged him together: "Deng Weigong, exploiting Wanrong's grave illness, has already seized control of the army and the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 今相公到此，尚不使人迎候，其情狀豈可料；

translations.literal: Now that the commissioner has arrived and still no one has been sent to welcome you, his intentions cannot be guessed;
translations.idiomatic: You have arrived and still no one comes to welcome you—his intentions are impossible to read;

sentences.zh: 即恐須且遲回，以候事勢。」

translations.literal: I fear you should delay and wait to see how matters develop."
translations.idiomatic: perhaps you should hold back and watch how events unfold."

sentences.zh: 晉曰：「奉詔為汴州節度使，即合準敕赴官，何可妄為逗留！」

translations.literal: Jin said: "I have been ordered Bian Prefecture military governor and should proceed to my post according to the edict—how can I recklessly linger!"
translations.idiomatic: Jin said, "I have been appointed military governor of Bian Prefecture. I must proceed to my post as the edict commands. How can I linger without cause!"

sentences.zh: 人皆憂其不測，晉獨恬然。

translations.literal: Everyone feared disaster for him, but Jin alone remained calm.
translations.idiomatic: All feared for him, but Jin alone remained untroubled.

sentences.zh: 未至汴州十數里，鄧惟恭方來迎候，晉俾其不下馬；

translations.literal: When he was still a dozen or so li from Bian Prefecture, Deng Weigong finally came to welcome him; Jin made him remain mounted;
translations.idiomatic: When he was still a dozen li from Bian Prefecture, Deng Weigong at last came to meet him. Jin would not let him dismount;

sentences.zh: 既入，乃委惟恭以軍政，眾服晉明於事體機變，而未測其深淺。

translations.literal: once inside, he entrusted military affairs to Weigong; the masses admired Jin's grasp of circumstances and adaptability, yet could not fathom his depth.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside the city he entrusted military affairs to Weigong. The troops admired Jin's grasp of the situation, yet could not gauge how deep his design ran.

sentences.zh: 初，萬榮逐劉士寧，代為節度使，委兵於惟恭，以其同鄉里。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wanrong drove out Liu Shining and replaced him as military governor, he entrusted the army to Weigong because they were from the same village.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wanrong drove out Liu Shining and took his place as military governor, he entrusted the troops to Weigong because they were fellow villagers.

sentences.zh: 及疾甚，李乃將為亂，惟恭乃與監軍同謀縛乃，送歸朝廷。

translations.literal: When Wanrong fell gravely ill, Li Nai was about to raise a disturbance; Weigong then conspired with the army supervisor to bind Nai and send him to the court.
translations.idiomatic: When Wanrong fell gravely ill and Li Nai was about to rebel, Weigong conspired with the army supervisor to bind Nai and send him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 惟恭自以當便代居其位，故不遣候吏，以疑懼晉心，冀其不敢進。

translations.literal: Weigong thought he would naturally succeed to the post, so he did not send welcoming officers, hoping to frighten Jin and make him dare not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Weigong expected to succeed Wanrong himself, so he sent no welcoming officers, hoping to intimidate Jin and keep him from advancing.

sentences.zh: 不意晉之速至。

translations.literal: He did not expect Jin to arrive so quickly.
translations.idiomatic: He did not expect Jin to arrive so swiftly.

sentences.zh: 晉已近，方遽出迎之。

translations.literal: When Jin was already near, he hurried out to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was already close at hand, he rushed out to meet him.

sentences.zh: 然心常怏怏，竟以驕盈慢法，潛圖不軌，配流嶺南。

translations.literal: Yet his heart was always resentful; in the end, for arrogant violation of law and secret plotting of rebellion, he was banished to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he remained resentful at heart. In the end, for arrogant defiance of law and secret plotting of rebellion, he was banished to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 朝廷恐晉柔懦，尋以汝州刺史陸長源為晉行軍司馬。

translations.literal: The court, fearing Jin was too mild, soon appointed Ru Prefect Lu Changyuan as Jin's army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Jin was too mild, the court soon appointed Ru Prefect Lu Changyuan as his army commander.

sentences.zh: 晉謙恭簡儉，每事因循多可，故亂兵粗安。

translations.literal: Jin was modest, respectful, and frugal; in most matters he followed precedent and assented, so the mutinous troops were roughly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was modest, respectful, and frugal; on most matters he followed precedent and assented, so the mutinous troops were roughly kept quiet.

sentences.zh: 長源好更張雲為，數請改易舊事，務從削刻。

translations.literal: Changyuan liked to change established practice and repeatedly asked to alter old arrangements, striving for harsh economies.
translations.idiomatic: Changyuan liked to overturn established ways and repeatedly sought to change old arrangements, pressing for harsh economies.

sentences.zh: 晉初皆然之，及案牘已成，晉乃命且罷。

translations.literal: At first Jin agreed to everything, but when the documents were already drawn up, Jin ordered them set aside for the time being.
translations.idiomatic: At first Jin agreed to everything, but once the documents were drafted he ordered them shelved.

sentences.zh: 又委錢谷支計於判官孟叔度。

translations.literal: He also entrusted fiscal accounts and disbursements to Administrative Aide Meng Shudu.
translations.idiomatic: He also entrusted fiscal accounts and disbursements to Administrative Aide Meng Shudu.

sentences.zh: 叔度輕佻，好慢易軍人，皆惡之。

translations.literal: Shudu was frivolous and liked to treat soldiers lightly; all hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Shudu was frivolous and treated soldiers with contempt; all hated him.

sentences.zh: 晉十五年二月卒，年七十六，廢朝三日，贈太傅，賜布帛有差。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifteenth year of Jin's tenure he died at age seventy-six; court was suspended three days; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor and given cloth and silk in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifteenth year Jin died at seventy-six. Court audiences were suspended for three days. He was posthumously ennobled Grand Tutor and granted graded gifts of cloth and silk.

sentences.zh: 卒後未十日，汴州大亂，殺長源、叔度等。

translations.literal: Within ten days after his death, Bian Prefecture fell into great disorder and Changyuan, Shudu, and others were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Less than ten days after his death Bian Prefecture erupted in chaos, and Changyuan, Shudu, and others were killed.

sentences.zh: 陸長源，字泳之，開元、天寶中尚書左丞、太子詹事余慶之孫，西河太守璪之子。

translations.literal: Lu Changyuan, courtesy name Yongzhi, was grandson of Yuqing, Left Vice Director of the Ministry and Household Steward to the Heir Apparent in the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, and son of Suo, prefect of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Changyuan, courtesy name Yongzhi, was grandson of Yuqing, who had served as Left Vice Director of the Ministry and Household Steward to the Heir Apparent under Emperors Kaiyuan and Tianbao, and son of Suo, prefect of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 長源淑書史。

translations.literal: Changyuan was versed in books and history.
translations.idiomatic: Changyuan was accomplished in literature and history.

sentences.zh: 乾元中，陷河北諸賊，因佐昭義軍節度薛嵩卒後。

translations.literal: In the Qianyuan era he was trapped in the rebel-held north and thereafter served the Zhaoyi army after Military Governor Xue Song's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianyuan era he was caught in the rebel-held north and afterward served under the Zhaoyi army after Military Governor Xue Song died.

sentences.zh: 久之，歷建、信二州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long while he successively served as prefect of Jian and Xin.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he served in succession as prefect of Jian and Xin.

sentences.zh: 浙西節度韓滉兼領江、淮轉運，奏長源檢校郎中、兼中丞，充轉運副使。

translations.literal: Zhexi Military Governor Han Huang also headed Jiang-Huai transport; he memorialized for Changyuan as acting Director and concurrent Censor-in-chief, serving as transport deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhexi Military Governor Han Huang also headed Jiang-Huai transport and memorialized for Changyuan as acting Director with concurrent Censor-in-chief, serving as transport deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 罷為都官郎中，改萬年縣令，出為汝州刺史。

translations.literal: He was relieved as Director of the Bureau of Punishments, changed to magistrate of Wannian County, and sent out as Ru prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was relieved as Director of the Bureau of Punishments, made magistrate of Wannian County, and then sent out as prefect of Ru.

sentences.zh: 貞元十二年，授檢校禮部尚書、宣武軍行軍司馬，汴州政事，皆決斷之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhenyuan he was appointed acting Minister of Rites and army commander of the Xuanwu army; Bian Prefecture government affairs were all decided by him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhenyuan he was appointed acting Minister of Rites and army commander of the Xuanwu army, and all affairs of Bian Prefecture were decided by him.

sentences.zh: 性輕佻，言論容易，恃才傲物，所在人畏而惡之。

translations.literal: His nature was frivolous; his speech was careless; he relied on talent and looked down on others; wherever he went people feared and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: He was frivolous by nature, careless in speech, arrogant in talent, and wherever he went people feared and despised him.

sentences.zh: 及至汴州，欲以峻法繩驕兵；

translations.literal: When he reached Bian Prefecture he wished to restrain the arrogant troops with harsh law;
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Bian Prefecture he meant to discipline the arrogant troops with harsh law;

sentences.zh: 而董晉判官楊凝、孟叔度亦縱恣淫湎，眾情共怒。

translations.literal: yet Dong Jin's administrative aides Yang Ning and Meng Shudu also indulged in dissipation and debauchery, and popular feeling was jointly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: but Dong Jin's administrative aides Yang Ning and Meng Shudu also indulged in dissipation and debauchery, and popular anger united against them.

sentences.zh: 晉性寬緩，事務因循，以收士心。

translations.literal: Jin's nature was lenient; affairs dragged on through precedent to win the troops' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was lenient by nature and let affairs drift along by precedent to win the troops' loyalty.

sentences.zh: 長源每事守法，晉或茍且，長源輒執而正之。

translations.literal: Changyuan enforced the law in every matter; when Jin was lax, Changyuan would seize on it and correct him.
translations.idiomatic: Changyuan enforced the law in every matter; whenever Jin was lax, Changyuan would seize on it and set him right.

sentences.zh: 及晉卒，令長源知留後事。

translations.literal: When Jin died, Changyuan was ordered to manage acting commission affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin died, Changyuan was left acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 長源揚言曰：「將士多弛慢，不守憲章，當以法繩之。」

translations.literal: Changyuan declared openly, "The officers and soldiers are mostly slack and do not keep the statutes; they must be restrained by law."
translations.idiomatic: He announced, "The troops are slack and lawless and must be disciplined."

sentences.zh: 由是人人恐懼。

translations.literal: Thereupon everyone was afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone was terrified.

sentences.zh: 加以叔度苛刻，多縱聲色，數至樂營與諸婦人嬉戲，自稱孟郎，眾皆薄之。

translations.literal: Added to this, Shudu was harsh; he indulged in music and women, often went to the music camp to sport with various women, called himself Master Meng, and all despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Shudu was harsh, chased women in the music camp, called himself Master Meng, and was despised.

sentences.zh: 舊例，使長薨，放散布帛於三軍制服。

translations.literal: By old custom, when a commissioner died, cloth and silk were distributed to the three armies for mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, when a commissioner died, cloth was issued to the army for mourning.

sentences.zh: 至是，人請服，長源初固不允，軍人求之不已，長源等議給其布直。

translations.literal: On this occasion the men asked for mourning dress; at first Changyuan firmly refused; the soldiers pressed unceasingly; Changyuan and the others discussed giving them cash in lieu of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The troops asked for mourning cloth; Changyuan refused, then offered cash instead.

sentences.zh: 叔度高其鹽價而賤為布直，每人不過得鹽三二斤，軍情大變。

translations.literal: Shudu raised the price of salt and cheapened the cash-for-cloth rate, so each man received no more than two or three jin of salt; army sentiment changed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Shudu inflated salt prices and cheated the cash payment—each man got only a few pounds of salt—and the army turned.

sentences.zh: 或勸長源，故事有大變，皆賞三軍，三軍乃安。

translations.literal: Some urged Changyuan that by precedent, when there is great upheaval, the three armies are always rewarded and then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged that custom required rewarding the army after upheaval to calm them.

sentences.zh: 長源曰：「不可使我同河北賊，以錢買健兒取旌節。」

translations.literal: Changyuan said, "I cannot let me be like the Hebei rebels, buying stalwart soldiers with money to seize the commander's banner and seal."
translations.idiomatic: Changyuan said, "I will not buy troops with money like the Hebei rebels to seize a commander's banner and seal."

sentences.zh: 兵士怨怒滋甚，乃執長源及叔度等臠而食之，斯須骨肉糜散。

translations.literal: The soldiers' resentment and rage grew ever worse; they seized Changyuan and Shudu and others, dismembered them, and ate them; in an instant flesh and bone were scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The enraged troops seized Changyuan and Shudu, dismembered them, and devoured them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 長源死之日，詔下以為節度使，及聞其死，中外惜之，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On the day Changyuan died an edict had just come down appointing him military governor; when his death was heard, inside and outside the court regretted it, and he was posthumously made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: The day he died his commission as governor arrived; the court mourned him and made him Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 劉全諒，懷州武涉人也。

translations.literal: Liu Quanliang was a native of Wushe in Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Quanliang came from Wushe in Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父客奴，由征行家於幽州之昌平。

translations.literal: His father Kerenu, through campaigning, established his household in Changping of You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kerenu, a campaigning soldier, had settled his household in Changping in You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少有武藝，從平盧軍。

translations.literal: In youth he had martial skill and joined the Pinglu army.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he had martial skill and joined the Pinglu army.

sentences.zh: 開元中，有室韋首領段普恪，恃驍勇，數苦邊。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era the Shiwei chieftain Duan Puke, relying on fierce courage, repeatedly harried the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era the Shiwei chieftain Duan Puke, trusting in his ferocity, repeatedly harassed the frontier.

sentences.zh: 節度使薛楚玉以客奴有膽氣，令抗普恪。

translations.literal: Military Governor Xue Chuyu, seeing Kerenu's bold spirit, ordered him to resist Puke.
translations.idiomatic: Military Governor Xue Chuyu, seeing Kerenu's courage, ordered him to oppose Puke.

sentences.zh: 客奴單騎襲之，斬首以獻，自白身授左驍衛將軍，充遊奕使，自是數有戰功。

translations.literal: Kerenu alone on horseback raided him, beheaded him and presented the head; from commoner status he was appointed General of the Left Xiaowei Guard, made roving patrol commissioner, and thereafter repeatedly won battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: Kerenu rode out alone, raided him, and presented his head. From commoner status he was appointed General of the Left Xiaowei Guard and made roving patrol commissioner, and thereafter won repeated battle honors.

sentences.zh: 性忠謹，為軍人所信。

translations.literal: His nature was loyal and careful, and the soldiers trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: He was loyal and careful by nature, and the troops trusted him.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，安祿山反，詔以安西節度封常清為范陽節度，以平盧節度副使呂知誨為平盧節度，以太原尹王承業為河東節度。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao, when An Lushan rebelled, the court ordered Anxi Military Governor Feng Changqing made Fanyang military governor, Pinglu Deputy Military Governor Lü Zhihui made Pinglu military governor, and Taiyuan Intendant Wang Chengye made Hedong military governor.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianbao, when An Lushan rebelled, the court appointed Anxi Military Governor Feng Changqing military governor of Fanyang, Pinglu Deputy Military Governor Lü Zhihui military governor of Pinglu, and Taiyuan Intendant Wang Chengye military governor of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 祿山既僭位於東都，遣腹心韓朝陽等招誘知誨；

translations.literal: After Lushan had usurped the throne in the eastern capital, he sent his trusted follower Han Chaoyang and others to entice Zhihui;
translations.idiomatic: After Lushan had proclaimed himself emperor in the eastern capital, he sent his trusted follower Han Chaoyang and others to win over Zhihui;

sentences.zh: 知誨遂受逆命，誘殺安東副都護、保定軍使馬靈詧，祿山遂署知誨為平盧節度使。

translations.literal: Zhihui then accepted the rebel commission, lured and killed Andong Deputy Protector-General and Baoding army commissioner Ma Lingzhe; Lushu then appointed Zhihui Pinglu military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhihui accepted the rebel commission, lured and killed Andong Deputy Protector-General and Baoding army commissioner Ma Lingzhe, and Lushan then appointed Zhihui military governor of Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 客奴與平盧諸將同議，取知誨殺之；

translations.literal: Kerenu consulted with the Pinglu generals and killed Zhihui;
translations.idiomatic: Kerenu consulted with the Pinglu generals, killed Zhihui,

sentences.zh: 仍遣與安東將王玄誌遙相應援，馳以奏聞。

translations.literal: still sent word to coordinate remotely with Andong general Wang Xuanzhi, and hurriedly reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: sent word to coordinate with Andong General Wang Xuanzhi, and hurriedly reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 十五載四月，授客奴柳城郡太守、攝御史大夫、平盧節度支度營田陸運、押兩蕃、渤海黑水四府經略及平盧軍使，仍賜名正臣。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifteenth year he was appointed Kerenu prefect of Liucheng Commandery, acting Grand Censor, Pinglu military governor with charge of garrison fields, land transport, and supervision of the two foreign offices and the four frontier commissions of Bohai and Heishui, and commissioner of the Pinglu army; he was also granted the name Zhengchen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifteenth year Kerenu was appointed prefect of Liucheng Commandery, acting Grand Censor, Pinglu military governor with charge of garrison fields, land transport, and supervision of the two foreign offices and the four frontier commissions of Bohai and Heishui, and commissioner of the Pinglu army; he was also granted the name Zhengchen.

sentences.zh: 又以王玄誌為安東副大都護、攝御史中丞、保定軍及營田使。

translations.literal: Wang Xuanzhi was also made Andong Deputy Grand Protector-General, acting Censor-in-chief, and commissioner of the Baoding army and garrison fields.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanzhi was also made Andong Deputy Grand Protector-General, acting Censor-in-chief, and commissioner of the Baoding army and garrison fields.

sentences.zh: 正臣仍領兵平盧來襲范陽，未至，為逆賊將史思明等大敗之。

translations.literal: Zhengchen still led Pinglu troops to strike Fanyang; before he arrived he was utterly defeated by the rebel general Shi Siming and others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengchen still led Pinglu troops to strike at Fanyang, but before he arrived he was utterly defeated by the rebel general Shi Siming and others.

sentences.zh: 正臣奔歸，為王玄誌所鴆而卒。

translations.literal: Zhengchen fled back and was poisoned to death by Wang Xuanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengchen fled back and was poisoned to death by Wang Xuanzhi.

sentences.zh: 逆賊署徐歸道平盧節度，王玄誌與平盧將侯希逸等又襲殺歸道。

translations.literal: The rebels appointed Xu Guidao Pinglu military governor; Wang Xuanzhi and Pinglu generals Hou Xiyi and others again attacked and killed Guidao.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels appointed Xu Guidao military governor of Pinglu; Wang Xuanzhi and Pinglu generals Hou Xiyi and others again attacked and killed Guidao.

sentences.zh: 大歷九年，追贈正臣工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dali, Zhengchen was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Dali, Zhengchen was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 全諒本名逸準，以父勛授別駕、長史。

translations.literal: Quanliang's original name was Yizhun; by his father's merit he was appointed vice prefect and chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Quanliang's original name was Yizhun; by his father's merit he was appointed vice prefect and chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 建中初，劉玄佐為宋亳節度使，召署為牙將，以勇果騎射聞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, when Liu Xuanzuo was Song-Bo military governor, he summoned him as a yajiang for his courage, horsemanship, and archery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianzhong, when Liu Xuanzuo was military governor of Song and Bo, he summoned Yizhun as a staff officer for his courage, horsemanship, and archery.

sentences.zh: 玄佐以宗侄厚遇之，累署都知兵馬使，試太仆卿、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: Xuanzuo, treating him as a clansman nephew, favored him generously and repeatedly appointed him overall commander of military affairs, acting Director of the Imperial Studs, and concurrent Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzuo treated him as a clansman nephew and favored him generously, repeatedly appointing him overall commander of military affairs, acting Director of the Imperial Studs, and concurrent Censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 玄佐卒，子士寧代為節度使，疑宋州刺史翟良佐不附己，陽言出巡，至宋州，遽以逸準代良佐為刺史。

translations.literal: When Xuanzuo died, his son Shining replaced him as military governor; suspecting Song Prefect Zhai Liangzuo of not submitting to him, he falsely announced an inspection tour, reached Song Prefecture, and abruptly replaced Liangzuo with Yizhun as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzuo died, his son Shining succeeded him as military governor. Suspecting Song Prefect Zhai Liangzuo of disloyalty, he announced an inspection tour, reached Song Prefecture, and abruptly replaced Liangzuo with Yizhun as prefect.

sentences.zh: 及董晉卒，兵亂，殺陸長源，監軍俱文珍與大將密召逸準赴汴州，令知留後。

translations.literal: When Dong Jin died and the troops mutinied, killing Lu Changyuan, Army Supervisor Ju Wenzhen and the great generals secretly summoned Yizhun to Bian Prefecture and ordered him to handle acting affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Jin died the army mutinied and killed Lu Changyuan. Army Supervisor Ju Wenzhen and the senior generals secretly summoned Yizhun to Bian Prefecture and put him in charge as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 朝廷因授以檢校工部尚書、汴州刺史，兼宣武軍節度觀察等使，仍賜名全諒。

translations.literal: The court thereupon appointed him acting Minister of Works, Bian prefect, and concurrent Xuanwu military governor and observation commissioner; he was also granted the name Quanliang.
translations.idiomatic: The court thereupon appointed him acting Minister of Works, prefect of Bian, and concurrent military governor and observation commissioner of the Xuanwu army; he was also granted the name Quanliang.

sentences.zh: 貞元十五年二月卒，年四十九，廢朝一日，贈右僕射。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan he died at age forty-nine; court was suspended one day; he was posthumously made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan he died at forty-nine. Court audiences were suspended for one day, and he was posthumously made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 李忠臣，本姓董，名秦，平盧人也，世家於幽州薊縣。

translations.literal: Li Zhongchen, original surname Dong, original name Qin, was a native of Pinglu and his family had long been established in Jixian of You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongchen, original surname Dong and original name Qin, was a man of Pinglu whose family had long been established in Jixian in You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 自雲曾祖文昱，棣州刺史；

translations.literal: He himself said his great-great-grandfather Wenyü was prefect of Di;
translations.idiomatic: He claimed that his great-great-grandfather Wenyü had been prefect of Di;

sentences.zh: 祖玄獎，安東都護府錄事參軍；

translations.literal: his great-grandfather Xuanjiang was recording secretary of the Andong protectorate;
translations.idiomatic: that his great-grandfather Xuanjiang had been recording secretary of the Andong protectorate;

sentences.zh: 父神嶠，河內府折沖。

translations.literal: his father Shenqiao was commander of the Henan circuit defense force.
translations.idiomatic: and that his father Shenqiao had been commander of the Henan circuit defense force.

sentences.zh: 忠臣少從軍，在卒伍之中，材力冠異。

translations.literal: Zhongchen joined the army young; among the ranks his strength and ability were foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen entered the army young; among the ranks his strength and ability stood foremost.

sentences.zh: 事幽州節度薛楚玉、張守珪、安祿山等，頻委征討，積勞至折沖郎將、將軍同正、平盧軍先鋒使。

translations.literal: He served You Prefecture military governors Xue Chuyu, Zhang Shougui, An Lushan, and others, was repeatedly entrusted with campaigns, and through accumulated merit rose to commander of the defense force, general with concurrent status, and vanguard commissioner of the Pinglu army.
translations.idiomatic: He served under You Prefecture military governors Xue Chuyu, Zhang Shougui, An Lushan, and others, was repeatedly sent on campaign, and through accumulated merit rose to commander of the defense force, general with concurrent status, and vanguard commissioner of the Pinglu army.

sentences.zh: 及祿山反，與其倫輩密議，殺偽節度呂知誨，立劉正臣為節度，以忠臣為兵馬使。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, he secretly discussed with his peers, killed the false military governor Lü Zhihui, installed Liu Zhengchen as military governor, and made Zhongchen army commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled he secretly discussed with his comrades, killed the puppet military governor Lü Zhihui, installed Liu Zhengchen as military governor, and made Zhongchen army commissioner.

sentences.zh: 攻長楊，戰獨山，襲榆關、北平，殺賊將申子貢、榮先欽，擒周釗送京師，忠臣功多。

translations.literal: He attacked Changyang, fought at Dushan, raided Yuguan and Beiping, killed the rebel generals Shen Zigong and Rong Xianqin, captured Zhou Zhao and sent him to the capital—Zhongchen's merit was great.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Changyang, fought at Dushan, raided Yuguan and Beiping, killed the rebel generals Shen Zigong and Rong Xianqin, captured Zhou Zhao and sent him to the capital—Zhongchen's achievements were many.

sentences.zh: 又從正臣破漁陽，逆將李歸仁、李鹹、白秀芝等來拒戰，約數十合，並摧破之；

translations.literal: He also followed Zhengchen in breaking Yuyang; the rebel generals Li Guiren, Li Xian, Bai Xiuzhi, and others came to resist; after some thirty engagements all were crushed;
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Zhengchen in taking Yuyang. The rebel generals Li Guiren, Li Xian, Bai Xiuzhi, and others came to resist; after some thirty engagements all were crushed;

sentences.zh: 無何，潼關失守，郭子儀、李光弼退師，忠臣乃引軍北歸。

translations.literal: before long Tong Pass fell; Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi withdrew their armies, and Zhongchen then led his troops north in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Tong Pass fell. Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi withdrew, and Zhongchen led his army back north.

sentences.zh: 奚王阿篤孤初以眾與正臣合，後詐言請以萬余騎同收范陽，至後城南，中夜反攻，忠臣與戰，遂至溫泉山，破之；

translations.literal: The Xi chieftain Adugu at first joined forces with Zhengchen; later he falsely said he would bring more than ten thousand horsemen to recover Fanyang together; when they reached the south of the rear city at midnight he turned and attacked; Zhongchen fought him and pursued to Wenquan Mountain and defeated him;
translations.idiomatic: The Xi chieftain Adugu at first joined Zhengchen with his forces, then falsely offered more than ten thousand horsemen to recover Fanyang together. At midnight south of the rear city he turned and attacked. Zhongchen fought him, pursued to Wenquan Mountain, and defeated him;

sentences.zh: 擒大首領阿布離，斬以祭纛釁鼓。

translations.literal: he captured the great chieftain Abu Li and beheaded him to sacrifice before the banners and drums.
translations.idiomatic: he captured the great chieftain Abu Li and beheaded him to sacrifice before the banners and drums.

sentences.zh: 正臣卒，又與眾議以安東都護王玄誌為節度使。

translations.literal: When Zhengchen died, he again consulted with the masses and made Andong Protector-General Wang Xuanzhi military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhengchen died he again consulted with the troops and made Andong Protector-General Wang Xuanzhi military governor.

sentences.zh: 至德二載正月，玄誌令忠臣以步卒三千自雍奴為葦筏過海。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Zhide, Xuanzhi ordered Zhongchen to take three thousand foot soldiers from Yongnu and cross the sea on reed rafts.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Zhide, Xuanzhi ordered Zhongchen to take three thousand foot soldiers from Yongnu and cross the sea on reed rafts.

sentences.zh: 賊將石帝庭、烏承洽來拒；

translations.literal: The rebel generals Shi Diting and Wu Chenghe came to resist;
translations.idiomatic: The rebel generals Shi Diting and Wu Chenghe came to resist;

sentences.zh: 忠臣與董竭忠退之，轉戰累日，遂收魯城、河間、景城等，大獲資糧，以赴本軍。

translations.literal: Zhongchen and Dong Jiezhong drove them back; after days of fighting he recovered Lucheng, Hejian, Jingcheng, and others, greatly obtaining provisions and grain to supply the main army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen and Dong Jiezhong drove them back. After days of fighting he recovered Lucheng, Hejian, Jingcheng, and others, greatly obtaining grain and supplies for the main army.

sentences.zh: 復與大將田神功率兵討平原、樂安郡，下之；

translations.literal: He again joined the great general Tian Shenggong in leading troops to subdue Pingyuan and Le'an commanderies and took them;
translations.idiomatic: He again joined the great general Tian Shenggong in leading troops to subdue the commanderies of Pingyuan and Le'an and took them;

sentences.zh: 擒偽刺史臧瑜等。

translations.literal: he captured the false prefect Zang Yu and others.
translations.idiomatic: he captured the puppet prefect Zang Yu and others.

sentences.zh: 防河招討使李銑承制以忠臣為德州刺史。

translations.literal: River-defense pacification commissioner Li Xian, by imperial commission, appointed Zhongchen prefect of De.
translations.idiomatic: River-defense pacification commissioner Li Xian, acting by imperial commission, appointed Zhongchen prefect of De.

sentences.zh: 屬史思明歸順，河南節度張鎬令忠臣以兵赴鄆州，與諸軍使收河南州縣。

translations.literal: When Shi Siming submitted to the court, Henan Military Governor Zhang Gao ordered Zhongchen to lead troops to Yan Prefecture and join the various army commissioners in recovering Henan prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming submitted, Henan Military Governor Zhang Gao ordered Zhongchen to march to Yan Prefecture and join the other commissioners in recovering the prefectures and counties of Henan.

sentences.zh: 又與裨將陽惠元大破賊將王福德於舒舍口，肅宗累下詔慰諭，仍令鎮濮州，尋移韋城。

translations.literal: He again joined Vice General Yang Huiyuan in utterly defeating the rebel general Wang Fude at Shushekou; Suzong repeatedly issued edicts of consolation, still ordered him to garrison Pu Prefecture, and soon moved him to Weicheng.
translations.idiomatic: With Vice General Yang Huiyuan he again routed the rebel general Wang Fude at Shushekou. Emperor Suzong repeatedly sent edicts of praise and ordered him to garrison Pu Prefecture, then soon moved him to Weicheng.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年九月，改光祿卿同正。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Qianyuan he was changed to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainment with concurrent status.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of Qianyuan he was made Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainment with concurrent status.

sentences.zh: 其年，與郭子儀等九節度圍安慶緒於相州。

translations.literal: That year he joined Guo Ziyi and eight other military governors in besieging An Qingxu at Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That year he joined Guo Ziyi and eight other military governors in besieging An Qingxu at Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，諸軍潰歸，忠臣亦退。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year the armies broke and retreated; Zhongchen also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year the allied armies broke and retreated; Zhongchen withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 至滎陽，賊將敬

translations.literal: When he reached Xingyang, the rebel general Jing
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Xingyang, the rebel general Jing

sentences.zh: 釭來襲官船，忠臣大破之，獲米二百余艘，以資汴州軍士。

translations.literal: Gang came to attack government boats; Zhongchen utterly defeated him, capturing more than two hundred grain boats to supply the troops of Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gang came to attack government transport boats. Zhongchen routed him and captured more than two hundred grain boats to supply the troops at Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尋拜濮州刺史、緣河守捉使，移鎮杏園渡。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Pu prefect and river-defense commissioner, and moved his garrison to Xingyuan Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed prefect of Pu and river-defense commissioner, and moved his garrison to Xingyuan Ford.

sentences.zh: 及史思明陷汴州，節度使許叔冀與忠臣並力屈降賊。

translations.literal: When Shi Siming took Bian Prefecture, Military Governor Xu Shuji and Zhongchen together, their strength exhausted, submitted to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming seized Bian Prefecture, Military Governor Xu Shuji and Zhongchen, their strength exhausted, submitted to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 思明撫忠臣背曰：「吾比只有左手，今得公，兼有右手矣！」

translations.literal: Siming stroked Zhongchen's back and said: "Before I had only a left hand; now that I have you, I have a right hand as well!"
translations.idiomatic: Siming clapped Zhongchen on the back and said, "Before I had only a left hand; now that I have you, I have a right hand as well!"

sentences.zh: 與俱寇河陽。

translations.literal: He joined him in raiding Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He joined him in raiding Heyang.

sentences.zh: 數日，忠臣夜以五百人斫其營，突圍歸。

translations.literal: Several days later, Zhongchen at night with five hundred men cut into their camp and broke out to return.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later Zhongchen took five hundred men by night, raided their camp, and broke out to return.

sentences.zh: 李光弼以聞，詔加開府儀同三司、殿中監同正，賜實封二百戶。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi reported it; the court added Opening the Mansion with Equal Third Rank and Director of the Palace Armory with concurrent status, and granted an enfeoffment of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi reported this. The court added Opening the Mansion with Equal Third Rank and Director of the Palace Armory with concurrent status, and granted an enfeoffment of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 召至京師，賜姓李氏，名忠臣，封隴西郡公，賜良馬、莊宅、銀器、彩物等。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the capital, granted the surname Li and the name Zhongchen, enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi, and given fine horses, estates, silver vessels, colored goods, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital, granted the surname Li and the name Zhongchen, enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi, and given fine horses, estates, silver vessels, and colored goods.

sentences.zh: 時陜西、神策兩節度郭英乂、衛伯玉鎮陜州，以忠臣為兩軍節度兵馬使。

translations.literal: At the time the two circuits of Shaanxi and Shence—Guo Yingyi and Wei Boyu—garrisoned Shaan Prefecture; Zhongchen was made army commander for both armies of the military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yingyi and Wei Boyu of Shaanxi and Shence circuits held Shaan; Li Zhongchen was made joint army commander.

sentences.zh: 魚朝恩亦在陜，俾忠臣與賊將李歸仁、李感義等戰於永寧、莎柵；

translations.literal: Yu Chaoen was also at Shaan; he had Zhongchen fight the rebel generals Li Guiren, Li Ganyi, and others at Yongning and Shazha;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chaoen in Shaan sent Li Zhongchen against Li Guiren, Li Ganyi, and other rebels at Yongning and Shazha;

sentences.zh: 前後數十陣，皆摧破之。

translations.literal: In front and behind, in some dozens of battles, all were crushed and broken.
translations.idiomatic: crushing them in dozens of battles.

sentences.zh: 會淮西節度王仲升為賊所擒，寶應元年七月，拜忠臣太常卿同正、兼御史中丞、淮西十一州節度。

translations.literal: At the time Huai-Xi military governor Wang Zhongsheng was captured by rebels; in the seventh month of the first year of Baoying, Zhongchen was appointed Minister of Ceremonies with honorary regular status, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, and military governor of the eleven prefectures of Huai-Xi.
