translations.idiomatic: When Huai-Xi governor Wang Zhongsheng was captured, in seventh month, Baoying 1, Li Zhongchen became Minister of Ceremonies, Censor-in-Chief, and governor of eleven Huai-Xi prefectures.

sentences.zh: 尋加安州刺史，仍鎮蔡州。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made prefect of An Prefecture, still garrisoning Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He soon added An prefect and kept his seat at Cai.

sentences.zh: 其年，令忠臣會元帥諸軍收復東都。

translations.literal: That year, he was ordered to join the field marshal's various armies in recovering the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: That year he joined the commander-in-chief's forces in retaking the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 二年六月，就加御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year, he was immediately advanced to Censor Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: In sixth month of year two he was promoted Censor Grandee.

sentences.zh: 時回紇可汗既歸其國，留判官安恪、石帝庭於河陽守禦財物，因此招聚亡命為寇，道路壅隔，詔忠臣討平之。

translations.literal: At the time the Uyghur qaghan had already returned to his state, leaving judicial officers An Ke and Shi Diting at Heyang to guard stored goods; on this account they gathered fugitives to become bandits, and the roads were blocked and cut off; an edict ordered Zhongchen to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghur qaghan had gone home but left An Ke and Shi Diting at Heyang to guard plunder; they recruited outlaws and cut the roads, so Li Zhongchen was ordered to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，吐蕃犯西陲，京師戒嚴。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, Tibet invaded the western frontier; the capital was placed under martial law.
translations.idiomatic: Yongtai 1 Tibet struck the western border and the capital went on alert.

sentences.zh: 代宗命中使追兵，諸道多不時赴難。

translations.literal: Daizong ordered palace emissaries to rush troops; the various circuits mostly did not come to the rescue in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong sent palace envoys to hurry reinforcements, but most circuits failed to come promptly.

sentences.zh: 使至淮西，忠臣方會鞠，即令整師飾駕。

translations.literal: When the emissary reached Huai-Xi, Zhongchen was just holding a banquet; he immediately ordered the army assembled and harnesses prepared.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy reached Huai-Xi, Li Zhongchen was at a banquet but immediately ordered his army mounted and ready.

sentences.zh: 監軍大將固請曰：「軍行須擇吉日。」

translations.literal: The army supervisor great general firmly requested, saying, "An army march must choose an auspicious day."
translations.idiomatic: The supervising general insisted, "We must pick an auspicious day to march."

sentences.zh: 忠臣奮臂於眾曰：「焉有父母遇寇難，待揀好日，方救患乎！」

translations.literal: Zhongchen raised his arm before the assembly and said, "How can it be that when one's parents meet bandit calamity, one waits to pick a good day before rescuing them from disaster!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongchen threw up his arm before the troops: "When your parents are under attack, do you wait for a lucky day to save them?"

sentences.zh: 即日進發。

translations.literal: That very day they advanced and set out.
translations.idiomatic: They marched that same day.

sentences.zh: 自此方隅有警，忠臣必先期而至。

translations.literal: From this time on, whenever the border regions had an alarm, Zhongchen always arrived ahead of the expected time.
translations.idiomatic: After that, whenever trouble broke out on the frontiers, Li Zhongchen arrived ahead of schedule.

sentences.zh: 由是代宗嘉其忠節，加本道觀察使，寵賜頗厚。

translations.literal: Because of this Daizong praised his loyalty and integrity, added him as observation commissioner of his own circuit, and favored and bestowed upon him quite generously.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong rewarded his loyalty with the circuit observation commission and rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 及同華節度周智光舉兵反，詔忠臣與神策將李太清等討平之。

translations.literal: When Tong-Hua military governor Zhou Zhiguang raised troops in rebellion, an edict ordered Zhongchen and Shence general Li Taiqing and others to suppress and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Zhiguang of Tong-Hua rebelled, Li Zhongchen and Shence general Li Taiqing were sent to crush him.

sentences.zh: 大歷三年，加檢校工部尚書，實封通前三百戶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dali, he was additionally made acting Minister of Works, with a cumulative enfeoffment through the prior grants of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Dali 3 brought acting Minister of Works and three hundred cumulative tax households.

sentences.zh: 五年，加蔡州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was additionally made prefect of Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he added Cai prefect.

sentences.zh: 七年，檢校右僕射、知省事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, acting Right Vice Director, in charge of Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Year seven he became acting Right Vice Director in charge of Secretariat business.

sentences.zh: 李靈曜之叛，田承嗣使侄悅援之，忠臣與諸軍大破悅等，汴州平。

translations.literal: When Li Lingyao rebelled, Tian Chengsi sent his nephew Yue to aid him; Zhongchen with the various armies greatly defeated Yue and the others, and Bian Prefecture was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Lingyao rebelled and Tian Chengsi's nephew Yue came to aid him, Li Zhongchen and the allies routed Yue and pacified Bian.

sentences.zh: 十一年十二月，加檢校司空平章事、汴州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the eleventh year, he was additionally made acting Minister of Works, co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and prefect of Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, year eleven, he became acting Minister of Works, co-director, and Bian prefect.

sentences.zh: 忠臣性貪殘好色，將吏妻女多被誘脅以通之。

translations.literal: Zhongchen's nature was greedy, cruel, and lustful; many officers' and officials' wives and daughters were enticed or coerced into relations with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen was greedy, cruel, and lustful; many officers' and officials' wives and daughters were enticed or coerced into sleeping with him.

sentences.zh: 又軍無紀綱，所至縱暴，人不堪命。

translations.literal: Moreover the army had no discipline; wherever he went he allowed violence, and people could not endure it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover his army had no discipline; wherever he went he allowed violence, and the people could not endure it.

sentences.zh: 而以妹婿張惠光為衙將，恃勢兇虐，軍中苦之；

translations.literal: Yet he made his brother-in-law Zhang Huiguang a guard officer; relying on his power he was brutal, and the army suffered from him;
translations.idiomatic: He made his brother-in-law Zhang Huiguang a guard officer. Huiguang relied on his power and was brutal, and the army suffered under him;

sentences.zh: 數有言於忠臣，不之信也。

translations.literal: many spoke of this to Zhongchen, but he did not believe them.
translations.idiomatic: Many reported this to Zhongchen, but he would not believe them.

sentences.zh: 俄以惠光為節度副使，令惠光子為衙將，陵橫甚於其父。

translations.literal: Before long Huiguang was made deputy military governor; Huiguang's son was made a guard officer, more overbearing than his father.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Huiguang was made deputy military governor and his son made a guard officer, even more overbearing than his father.

sentences.zh: 忠臣所信任大將李希烈，素善騎射，群情所伏，因眾心之怒，以十四年三月，與少將丁皓、賈子華、監軍判官蔣知璋等舉兵斬惠光父子，以脅逐忠臣。

translations.literal: The great general Li Xilie, whom Zhongchen trusted, was skilled in horsemanship and archery and admired by the masses; relying on popular anger, in the third month of the fourteenth year he joined Junior Generals Ding Hao, Jia Zihua, Army Supervisor Administrative Aide Jiang Zhizhang, and others in raising troops to behead Huiguang and his son, thereby driving Zhongchen out.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie, the great general Zhongchen trusted, was skilled in horsemanship and archery and admired by the troops. Relying on popular anger, in the third month of the fourteenth year he joined Junior Generals Ding Hao, Jia Zihua, Army Supervisor Administrative Aide Jiang Zhizhang, and others in raising troops to behead Huiguang and his son and drive Zhongchen out.

sentences.zh: 單騎赴京師，朝廷方寵武臣，不之責也，依前檢校司空、平章事，留京師奉朝請。

translations.literal: Zhongchen rode alone to the capital; the court was then favoring military men and did not blame him, keeping him as before as acting Minister of Works and Associate Grand Councilor, remaining in the capital to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen rode alone to the capital. The court was then indulgent toward military men and did not blame him, keeping him as acting Minister of Works and Associate Grand Councilor to remain in the capital and attend court.

sentences.zh: 建中初，嘗因奏對，德宗謂之曰：「卿耳甚大，真貴人也。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, once when memorializing in audience, Dezong said to him: "Your ears are very large—you are truly a noble man."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianzhong, when memorializing in audience, Dezong said to him, "Your ears are very large—you are truly a noble man."

sentences.zh: 忠臣對曰：「臣聞驢耳甚大，龍耳甚小；

translations.literal: Zhongchen replied: "I have heard that donkeys' ears are very large and dragons' ears very small;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen replied, "I have heard that donkeys have very large ears and dragons very small ones;

sentences.zh: 臣耳雖大，乃驢耳也。」

translations.literal: though my ears are large, they are donkeys' ears."
translations.idiomatic: though my ears are large, they are only a donkey's."

sentences.zh: 上說之。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 時常侍張涉承恩用事，坐受財賄事露，帝將以法繩之——涉，即帝在春宮時侍講也。

translations.literal: At that time Regular Attendant Zhang She, enjoying imperial favor and wielding power, was exposed for accepting bribes; the emperor was about to punish him by law—She had been the emperor's lecturer when he was heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Regular Attendant Zhang She, enjoying favor and wielding power, was exposed for taking bribes. The emperor was about to punish him by law—She had been the emperor's lecturer when he was heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 忠臣奏曰：「陛下貴為天子，而先生以乏財抵法，以愚臣觀之，非先生之過也。」

translations.literal: Zhongchen memorialized: "Your Majesty is exalted as Son of Heaven, yet the teacher is punished for lack of funds—in this foolish subject's view, it is not the teacher's fault."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen memorialized, "Your Majesty is exalted as Son of Heaven, yet the teacher is punished for lack of funds. In this foolish subject's view, it is not the teacher's fault."

sentences.zh: 帝意解，但令歸田裏。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind eased, and he only ordered She to return to his village.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented and only ordered She to return to his village.

sentences.zh: 前湖南觀察辛京杲嘗以忿怒杖殺部曲，有司劾奏京杲殺人當死，從之。

translations.literal: Former Hunan Observation Commissioner Xin Jinggao had once in anger beaten a subordinate to death; the authorities impeached him, reporting that Jinggao should die for killing, and the court assented.
translations.idiomatic: Former Hunan Observation Commissioner Xin Jinggao had once beaten a subordinate to death in anger. The authorities impeached him for a capital crime, and the court assented.

sentences.zh: 忠臣奏曰：「京杲合死久矣！

translations.literal: Zhongchen memorialized: "Jinggao ought to have died long ago!
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen memorialized, "Jinggao ought to have died long ago!

sentences.zh: 儒生；

translations.literal: A Confucian scholar;
translations.idiomatic: A mere Confucian scholar—

sentences.zh: 上問之，對曰：「渠柏叔某於某處戰死，兄弟某於某處戰死，渠嘗從行，獨不死，是以知渠合死久矣。」」

translations.literal: the emperor asked about it, and he replied, 'His uncle Bo died in battle at such-and-such a place, his brothers died in battle at such-and-such places; he once followed on campaign and alone did not die—therefore I know he ought to have died long ago.'"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked him to explain, and he replied, 'His uncle Bo died in battle at such-and-such a place, his brothers at such-and-such places. He once followed on campaign and alone did not die—so I know he ought to have died long ago.'"

sentences.zh: 上亦憫然，不令加罪，改授王傅而已。

translations.literal: The emperor also felt compassion and did not add punishment, only changing his appointment to Royal Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved to pity and did not add punishment, only changing his appointment to Royal Tutor.

sentences.zh: 忠臣木強率直，不識書，不喜儒生；

translations.literal: Zhongchen was dull, obstinate, and blunt; he did not know books and disliked Confucian scholars;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen was dull, obstinate, and blunt. He could not read and disliked Confucian scholars;

sentences.zh: 及罷兵權，官位崇重，常郁郁不得誌。

translations.literal: when he lost military power and his office grew exalted, he was often depressed and could not achieve his aims.
translations.idiomatic: when he lost military power and his rank grew exalted, he was often depressed and frustrated.

sentences.zh: 及硃泚反，以為偽司空、兼侍中。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he was made false Minister of Works and concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he was made false Minister of Works and concurrent Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 泚率兵逼奉天，命忠臣京城留守。

translations.literal: Ci led troops to press Fengtian and ordered Zhongchen to remain as capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: Ci led troops against Fengtian and ordered Zhongchen to remain as regent of the capital.

sentences.zh: 泚敗，忠臣走樊川別業，李晟下將士擒忠臣至，系之有司。

translations.literal: When Ci was defeated, Zhongchen fled to his estate at Fanchuan; Li Sheng's subordinate officers seized Zhongchen and handed him to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: When Ci was defeated, Zhongchen fled to his estate at Fanchuan. Li Sheng's officers seized him and handed him to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 興元元年，並其子並誅斬之，時年六十九，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan he and his sons were all executed; he was then sixty-nine, and his household property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingyuan he and his sons were all executed. He was sixty-nine, and his household property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 李希烈，遼西人。

translations.literal: Li Xilie was a man of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie came from Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 父大定。

translations.literal: His father was Dading.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Dading.

sentences.zh: 希烈少從平盧軍，後隨李忠臣過海至河南。

translations.literal: Xilie joined the Pinglu army young and later followed Li Zhongchen across the sea to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie joined the Pinglu army as a youth and later followed Li Zhongchen across the sea to Henan.

sentences.zh: 寶應初，忠臣為淮西節度，署希烈為偏裨，累授將軍、試光祿卿、殿中監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoying, when Zhongchen was Huaixi military governor, he appointed Xilie a junior officer; he was repeatedly promoted to general, acting Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainment, and Director of the Palace Armory.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Baoying, when Zhongchen was military governor of Huaixi, he appointed Xilie a junior officer. Xilie rose through repeated promotions to general, acting Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainment, and Director of the Palace Armory.

sentences.zh: 忠臣兼領汴州，希烈為左廂都虞候，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Zhongchen also held Bian Prefecture, Xilie was left-wing chief commander and was added Opening the Mansion with Equal Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongchen also held Bian Prefecture, Xilie was made chief commander of the left wing and granted Opening the Mansion with Equal Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 大歷末，忠臣軍政不修，事多委妹婿張惠光，為押衙，弄權縱恣，人怨。

translations.literal: At the end of Dali, Zhongchen did not maintain military government; he entrusted most affairs to his brother-in-law Zhang Huiguang as yaya, who manipulated power and acted willfully, arousing popular resentment.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Dali Zhongchen neglected military government and entrusted most affairs to his brother-in-law Zhang Huiguang as yaya. Huiguang manipulated power and acted willfully, arousing resentment.

sentences.zh: 與少將丁皓等斬惠光父子，忠臣奔赴朝廷。

translations.literal: With Junior Generals Ding Hao and others he beheaded Huiguang and his son; Zhongchen fled to the court.
translations.idiomatic: With Junior Generals Ding Hao and others he beheaded Huiguang and his son, and Zhongchen fled to the court.

sentences.zh: 詔以忻王為淮西節度副大使，授希烈蔡州刺史、兼御史中丞、淮西節度留後，令滑亳節度李勉兼領汴州。

translations.literal: The court ordered the Prince of Xin as deputy ambassador of Huaixi military governorship and appointed Xilie Cai prefect, concurrent Censor-in-chief, and acting Huaixi military governor, ordering Hua-Bo Military Governor Li Mian also to hold Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed the Prince of Xin deputy ambassador of the Huaixi military governorship and made Xilie prefect of Cai with concurrent Censor-in-chief and acting military governor of Huaixi, ordering Hua-Bo Military Governor Li Mian also to hold Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位後月余，加御史大夫，充淮西節度支度營田觀察使，又改淮西節度淮寧軍以寵之。

translations.literal: A little more than a month after Dezong succeeded, he was added Grand Censor, made Huaixi military governor with charge of garrison fields and observation commissioner, and again changed the Huaixi army to the Huaining army as a mark of favor.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than a month after Dezong succeeded, Xilie was made Grand Censor, military governor of Huaixi with charge of garrison fields and observation commissioner, and the Huaixi army was renamed the Huaining army as a mark of favor.

sentences.zh: 建中元年，又加檢校禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong he was further made acting Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianzhong he was further made acting Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 會山南東道節度梁崇義拒捍朝命，迫脅使臣，二年六月，詔諸軍節度率兵討之；

translations.literal: When Shannan East Circuit Military Governor Liang Chongyi resisted the court's orders and coerced envoys, in the sixth month of the second year the court ordered the various military governors to lead troops to attack him;
translations.idiomatic: When Shannan East Circuit Military Governor Liang Chongyi defied the court and coerced envoys, in the sixth month of the second year the court ordered the military governors to lead troops against him;

sentences.zh: 加希烈南平郡王，兼漢北都知諸兵馬招撫處置使。

translations.literal: Xilie was added Prince of Nanping and made overall commander of Hanbei knowing all armies, pacification and disposition commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie was made Prince of Nanping and overall commander of Hanbei knowing all armies, pacification and disposition commissioner.

sentences.zh: 希烈破崇義眾，遂討平之。

translations.literal: Xilie broke Chongyi's forces and then pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie broke Chongyi's army and then pacified him.

sentences.zh: 錄希烈功，加檢校右僕射、同平章事，賜實封五百戶。

translations.literal: Recording Xilie's merit, he was added acting Right Vice Director and Associate Grand Councilor and granted an enfeoffment of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Recording his merit, the court added him acting Right Vice Director and Associate Grand Councilor and granted an enfeoffment of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 淄青節度李正己又謀不軌，三年秋，加希烈檢校司空，兼淄青兗鄆登萊齊等州節度支度營田、新羅、渤海兩蕃使，令討襲正己。

translations.literal: Zi-Qing Military Governor Li Zhengji also plotted disloyalty; in the autumn of the third year Xilie was added acting Minister of Works and made military governor with charge of garrison fields for Zi, Qing, Yan, Yan, Deng, Lai, Qi, and other prefectures, commissioner to the two foreign offices of Silla and Bohai, and ordered to attack Zhengji.
translations.idiomatic: Zi-Qing Military Governor Li Zhengji also plotted rebellion. In the autumn of the third year Xilie was made acting Minister of Works and military governor with charge of garrison fields for Zi, Qing, Yan, Yan, Deng, Lai, Qi, and other prefectures, commissioner to Silla and Bohai, and ordered to attack Zhengji.

sentences.zh: 希烈遂率所部三萬人移居許州，聲言遣使往青州招諭李納，其實潛與交通，又移牒汴州令備供擬，將與納同為亂。

translations.literal: Xilie then led his division of thirty thousand to move to Xu Prefecture, claiming he would send envoys to Qingzhou to win over Li Na, but in fact secretly communicating with him; he also sent a dispatch to Bian Prefecture ordering preparations, intending to rebel with Na.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie then led his thirty thousand men to Xu Prefecture, claiming he would send envoys to Qingzhou to win over Li Na while secretly communicating with him. He also sent a dispatch to Bian Prefecture demanding preparations, intending to rebel with Na.

sentences.zh: 李勉以其道路合自陳留，乃除道具饌以待之，希烈不從，乃大慢罵。

translations.literal: Li Mian, because his route ought to pass through Chenliu, prepared supplies and food to await him; Xilie would not follow and greatly reviled him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mian, because Xilie's route ought to pass through Chenliu, prepared supplies to await him. Xilie refused and reviled him harshly.

sentences.zh: 自是誌意縱肆，言多悖慢，日遣使交通河北諸賊帥等。

translations.literal: From this his ambition grew unrestrained; his words were mostly insolent, and daily he sent envoys to communicate with the rebel chiefs of Hebei and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: From this his ambition grew unrestrained. His words were mostly insolent, and daily he sent envoys to the rebel chiefs of Hebei and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 是歲長至日，硃滔、田悅、王武俊、李納各僭稱王，滔使至希烈，希烈亦僭稱建興王、天下都元帥。

translations.literal: That year on the winter solstice Zhu Tao, Tian Yue, Wang Wujun, and Li Na each usurped royal titles; Tao sent envoys to Xilie, and Xilie also usurped the title King of Jianxing and Commander-in-Chief of All Under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: That year on the winter solstice Zhu Tao, Tian Yue, Wang Wujun, and Li Na each usurped royal titles. Tao sent envoys to Xilie, and Xilie also proclaimed himself King of Jianxing and Commander-in-Chief of All Under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 四年，希烈遣其將襲陷汝州，執李元平而去，東都大擾亂。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Xilie sent his general to raid and take Ru Prefecture, seizing Li Yuanping and carrying him off; the eastern capital was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Xilie sent his general to raid Ru Prefecture, seized Li Yuanping, and carried him off. The eastern capital was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 朝廷猶為含容，遣太子太師顏真卿往宣慰。

translations.literal: The court still showed forbearance and sent Grand Preceptor Yan Zhenqing to offer consolation.
translations.idiomatic: The court still showed forbearance and sent Grand Preceptor Yan Zhenqing to offer consolation.

sentences.zh: 真卿發後數日，以龍武將軍哥舒曜為東都兼汝州行營兵馬節度。

translations.literal: Several days after Zhenqing set out, Dragon Martial General Geshu Yao was made eastern capital and Ru Prefecture field army military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Several days after Zhenqing set out, Dragon Martial General Geshu Yao was made military governor of the eastern capital and Ru Prefecture field army.

sentences.zh: 希烈既見真卿，但肆兇言，令左右慢罵，指斥朝廷。

translations.literal: Once Xilie saw Zhenqing, he only uttered violent words, ordered his attendants to revile him, and denounced the court.
translations.idiomatic: When Xilie saw Zhenqing he only uttered violent threats, ordered his attendants to revile him, and denounced the court.

sentences.zh: 又遣逆黨董待名、韓霜露、劉敬宗、陳質、翟暉等四人伺外，侵抄州縣，官軍皆為其所敗，荊南節度張伯儀全軍覆沒。

translations.literal: He also sent his rebel followers Dong Daiming, Han Shuanglu, Liu Jingzong, Chen Zhi, Zhai Hui, and four others to watch outside, raiding prefectures and counties; government troops were all defeated by them, and Jingnan Military Governor Zhang Boyi lost his entire army.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent rebel followers Dong Daiming, Han Shuanglu, Liu Jingzong, Chen Zhi, Zhai Hui, and four others to raid prefectures and counties. Government troops were repeatedly defeated, and Jingnan Military Governor Zhang Boyi lost his entire army.

sentences.zh: 又令周曾、王玢、姚憺、呂從賁、康琳等來襲曜，曾、玢、憺等謀回軍據蔡州襲討希烈，事泄，並遇害。

translations.literal: He also ordered Zhou Zeng, Wang Bin, Yao Dan, Lü Congbin, Kang Lin, and others to attack Yao; Zeng, Bin, Dan, and others plotted to turn the army, hold Cai Prefecture, and strike at Xilie; the affair was exposed and they were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Zhou Zeng, Wang Bin, Yao Dan, Lü Congbin, Kang Lin, and others to attack Yao. Zeng, Bin, and Dan plotted to turn the army, seize Cai Prefecture, and strike at Xilie. The plot was exposed and they were all killed.

sentences.zh: 神策軍使白誌貞又獻策謀，令嘗為節度、都團練使者各出家僮部曲一人及馬，令劉德信總之討希烈。

translations.literal: Shence Army Commissioner Bai Zhizhen also offered a stratagem, ordering each former military governor and defense commissioner to contribute one household slave, retainer, and horse, and putting Liu Dexin in overall command to attack Xilie.
translations.idiomatic: Shence Army Commissioner Bai Zhizhen also offered a plan: each former military governor and defense commissioner was to contribute one household slave, retainer, and horse, with Liu Dexin in overall command against Xilie.

sentences.zh: 尋詔李勉為淮西招討使，哥舒曜為副。

translations.literal: Soon the court ordered Li Mian Huaixi pacification commissioner and Geshu Yao deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the court ordered Li Mian Huaixi pacification commissioner and Geshu Yao his deputy.

sentences.zh: 至四月，曜率眾屯襄城，頻與賊戰，皆不勝。

translations.literal: By the fourth month Yao led the masses to encamp at Xiangcheng; he repeatedly fought the rebels and was never victorious.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth month Yao encamped at Xiangcheng and repeatedly fought the rebels without victory.

sentences.zh: 八月，希烈率眾二萬圍襄城，李勉又令將唐漢臣率兵與劉德信同為曜之影援，皆望風敗衄。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Xilie led twenty thousand to besiege Xiangcheng; Li Mian again ordered General Tang Hanchen to lead troops with Liu Dexin as Yao's supporting force; all fled at the sight of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Xilie besieged Xiangcheng with twenty thousand men. Li Mian ordered General Tang Hanchen and Liu Dexin to support Yao; all fled at sight of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 希烈兇逆既甚，帝乃命舒王為荊襄、江西、沔鄂等道節度諸軍行營兵馬都元帥，大開幕府，文武僚屬之盛，前後出師，未有其比。

translations.literal: Xilie's rebellion had grown extreme; the emperor then ordered the Prince of Shu overall marshal of the Jing-Xiang, Jiangxi, Mian-E, and other circuits' field armies; he opened a grand headquarters, and the splendor of civil and military staff exceeded any prior campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie's rebellion had grown extreme. The emperor ordered the Prince of Shu overall marshal of the Jing-Xiang, Jiangxi, Mian-E, and other field armies and opened a grand headquarters whose civil and military staff exceeded any prior campaign.

sentences.zh: 又令涇原諸道出兵，皆赴襄城。

translations.literal: He also ordered the Jingyuan and other circuits to send troops, all proceeding to Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Jingyuan and other circuits to send troops to Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 軍未發，會涇州兵亂，車駕幸奉天。

translations.literal: Before the army set out, the Jingzhou troops mutinied and the imperial carriage went to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army set out, the Jingzhou troops mutinied and the emperor fled to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 其日，希烈大破曜軍於襄城，曜遁歸東都，賊因乘勝攻陷汴州，李勉奔歸宋州。

translations.literal: That day Xilie utterly defeated Yao's army at Xiangcheng; Yao fled back to the eastern capital, and the rebels pressed their advantage to take Bian Prefecture; Li Mian fled back to Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That day Xilie routed Yao at Xiangcheng. Yao fled to the eastern capital, the rebels pressed on to take Bian Prefecture, and Li Mian fled to Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 希烈性慘毒酷，每對戰陣殺人，流血盈前，而言笑飲饌自若，以此人畏而服從其教令，盡其死力。

translations.literal: Xilie's nature was cruel and poisonous; in battle he killed men until blood filled the ground before him, yet he spoke and laughed and ate and drank as if at ease; thereby people feared him and obeyed his commands, exerting their utmost strength.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie was cruel and vicious. In battle he killed until blood pooled before him, yet he spoke, laughed, ate, and drank as if at ease. Men feared him and obeyed his commands to the death.

sentences.zh: 其攻汴州，驅百姓，令運木土築壘道，又怒其未就，乃驅以填之，謂之濕梢。

translations.literal: When he attacked Bian Prefecture he drove the common people to transport timber and earth to build ramp paths; angered that the work was not done, he drove them to fill it in, calling this "wet timbers."
translations.idiomatic: When he attacked Bian Prefecture he drove civilians to haul timber and earth for siege ramps. Angered that the work lagged, he drove them to fill the ramps with their bodies, calling it "wet timbers."

sentences.zh: 既入汴州，於是僭號曰武成，以孫廣、鄭賁、李綬、李元平為宰相；

translations.literal: Once he entered Bian Prefecture he thereupon usurped the title Wucheng and made Sun Guang, Zheng Ben, Li Shou, and Li Yuanping chancellors;
translations.idiomatic: Once inside Bian Prefecture he usurped the reign title Wucheng and made Sun Guang, Zheng Ben, Li Shou, and Li Yuanping his chancellors;

sentences.zh: 以汴州為大梁府，李清虛為尹，署百官。

translations.literal: he made Bian Prefecture the capital Daliang, Li Qingxu prefect, and appointed the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: he made Bian the capital Daliang, appointed Li Qingxu prefect, and installed the full bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 遣兵東討，至寧陵，竟為劉洽所拒，不得前。

translations.literal: He sent troops east to attack; reaching Ningling, he was blocked by Liu Qia and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: He sent troops eastward; at Ningling he was blocked by Liu Qia and could not advance.

sentences.zh: 又遣將翟暉率精卒襲陳州，為劉洽、李納大破之，生擒暉以獻。

translations.literal: He again sent General Zhai Hui with elite troops to raid Chen Prefecture; Liu Qia and Li Na utterly defeated them and captured Hui alive to present.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent General Zhai Hui with elite troops to raid Chen Prefecture. Liu Qia and Li Na routed them and captured Hui alive.

sentences.zh: 諸軍乘勝進攻汴州，希烈遁歸蔡州，擒其偽署將相鄭賁、劉敬宗等。

translations.literal: The various armies pressed the attack on Bian Prefecture in victory; Xilie fled back to Cai Prefecture, and they captured his false appointees Zheng Ben, Liu Jingzong, and others.
translations.idiomatic: The allied armies pressed the attack on Bian Prefecture. Xilie fled to Cai Prefecture, and they captured his false chancellor Zheng Ben, Liu Jingzong, and others.

sentences.zh: 李臯、樊澤、曲環、張建封又四面討襲之，累拔其郡縣，希烈敗衄。

translations.literal: Li Gao, Fan Ze, Qu Huan, and Zhang Jianfeng also attacked him from four sides, repeatedly taking his prefectures and counties; Xilie was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao, Fan Ze, Qu Huan, and Zhang Jianfeng also attacked from four sides, repeatedly taking his prefectures and counties, and Xilie was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年三月，因食牛肉遇疾，其將陳仙奇令醫人陳仙甫置藥以毒之而死。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Zhenyuan, eating beef he fell ill; his general Chen Xianqi had the physician Chen Xianfu prepare medicine and poisoned him to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Zhenyuan he fell ill after eating beef. His general Chen Xianqi had the physician Chen Xianfu poison him to death.

sentences.zh: 妻男骨肉兄弟共一十七人，並誅之。

translations.literal: His wife, sons, flesh-and-blood brothers—seventeen persons in all—were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, sons, and brothers—seventeen persons in all—were all executed.

sentences.zh: 初，希烈於唐州得象一頭，以為瑞應，又上蔡、襄城獲其珍寶，乃是爛車釭及滑石偽印也。

translations.literal: Earlier Xilie had obtained an elephant at Tang Prefecture and regarded it as an auspicious sign; also at Shangcai and Xiangcheng he obtained what he thought were treasures, which were in fact rotten cart hubs and talc false seals.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xilie had obtained an elephant at Tang Prefecture and took it for an omen. At Shangcai and Xiangcheng he obtained what he thought were treasures, which proved to be rotten cart hubs and talc false seals.

sentences.zh: 陳仙奇者，起於行間，性忠果。

translations.literal: Chen Xianqi rose from the ranks; his nature was loyal and resolute.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianqi rose from the ranks; he was loyal and resolute by nature.

sentences.zh: 自希烈死，朝廷授淮西節度，頗竭誠節。

translations.literal: From Xilie's death the court appointed him Huaixi military governor, and he showed considerable loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: After Xilie's death the court appointed him military governor of Huaixi, and he showed considerable loyalty.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為別將吳少誠所殺，贈太子太保，賻布帛、米粟有差，喪事官給。

translations.literal: Before long he was killed by Vice General Wu Shaocheng; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent, given graded gifts of cloth, silk, and grain, and his funeral expenses were provided by the state.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was killed by Vice General Wu Shaocheng. He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent, given graded gifts of cloth, silk, and grain, and his funeral was provided by the state.

sentences.zh: 吳少誠，幽州潞縣人。

translations.literal: Wu Shaocheng was a native of Lu County in You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shaocheng came from Lu County in You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父為魏博節度都虞候。

translations.literal: His father was chief commander of the Weibo military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: His father had been chief commander of the Weibo military governorship.

sentences.zh: 少誠以父勛授一子官，釋褐王府戶曹。

translations.literal: Shaocheng by his father's merit was granted one son an office; he began service as Household Registrar of the Princely Establishment.
translations.idiomatic: By his father's merit Shaocheng was granted an office for one son; he began service as Household Registrar of the Princely Establishment.

sentences.zh: 後至荊南，節度使庾準奇之，留為衙門將。

translations.literal: Later he went to Jingnan; Military Governor Yu Zhun was impressed with him and kept him as a guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went to Jingnan. Military Governor Yu Zhun was impressed with him and kept him as a guard officer.

sentences.zh: 準入覲，從至襄漢，見梁崇義不遵憲度，知有異志，少誠密計有成擒之略，將自陳於闕下。

translations.literal: When Zhun went to audience, Shaocheng followed him to Xiang-Han, saw Liang Chongyi not observing the laws, knew he had a different intent, and secretly devised a plan to capture him, intending to report it at court himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhun went to audience Shaocheng followed him to Xiang-Han, saw Liang Chongyi defying the laws, knew he harbored rebellion, and secretly devised a plan to capture him, intending to report it at court.

sentences.zh: 屬李希烈初授節制，銳意立功，見少誠計慮，乃以少誠所見錄奏，有詔慰飭，不次封通義郡王。

translations.literal: When Li Xilie was first granted his commission and was eager to achieve merit, seeing Shaocheng's plans he memorialized what Shaocheng had observed; there was an edict of consolation and extraordinary enfeoffment as Prince of Tongyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie was first commissioned and eager for merit, he saw Shaocheng's plans, memorialized them, and the court issued an edict of praise and extraordinarily enfeoffed him as Prince of Tongyi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，崇義違命，希烈受制專征，以少誠為前鋒。

translations.literal: Before long Chongyi defied orders; Xilie received special command for the campaign and made Shaocheng vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chongyi defied orders. Xilie received special command for the campaign and made Shaocheng his vanguard.

sentences.zh: 崇義平，賜實封五千戶。

translations.literal: When Chongyi was pacified, he was granted an enfeoffment of five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongyi was pacified he was granted an enfeoffment of five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 後希烈叛，少誠頗為其用。

translations.literal: Later when Xilie rebelled, Shaocheng served him considerably.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Xilie rebelled, Shaocheng served him considerably.

sentences.zh: 希烈死，少誠等初推陳仙奇統戎事，朝廷已命仙奇，尋為少誠所殺，眾推少誠知留務。

translations.literal: When Xilie died, Shaocheng and others at first pushed Chen Xianqi to command military affairs; the court had already appointed Xianqi, but soon Shaocheng killed him and the masses pushed Shaocheng to handle acting affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xilie died, Shaocheng and others first pushed Chen Xianqi to command the army. The court had already appointed Xianqi, but soon Shaocheng killed him and the troops pushed Shaocheng to handle acting affairs.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遂授以申光蔡等州節度觀察兵馬留後，尋正授節度。

translations.literal: The court thereupon appointed him acting military governor and observation commissioner of Shen, Guang, Cai, and other prefectures; soon he was given the full commission.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed him acting military governor and observation commissioner of Shen, Guang, Cai, and other prefectures, and soon gave him the full commission.

sentences.zh: 少誠善為治，勤儉無私，日事完聚，不奉朝廷。

translations.literal: Shaocheng was skilled in administration, diligent and frugal without selfishness, daily strengthening his holdings, and did not serve the court.
translations.idiomatic: Shaocheng governed well, was diligent and frugal without selfishness, daily strengthened his holdings, and did not defer to the court.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，判官鄭常及大將楊冀謀逐少誠以聽命於朝，試校書郎劉涉假為手詔數十，潛致於大將，欲因少誠之出，閉城門以拒之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan Administrative Aide Zheng Chang and great general Yang Ji plotted to drive out Shaocheng so as to obey the court; Trial Proofreader Liu She forged several dozen handwritten edicts and secretly sent them to the great generals, intending when Shaocheng went out to close the city gates and resist him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenyuan Administrative Aide Zheng Chang and great general Yang Ji plotted to drive out Shaocheng and submit to the court. Trial Proofreader Liu She forged several dozen handwritten edicts and secretly sent them to the generals, intending when Shaocheng went out to close the gates and resist him.

sentences.zh: 屬少誠將出餞中使，常、冀等遂謀舉事；

translations.literal: As Shaocheng was about to go out to feast the imperial envoy, Chang, Ji, and others then plotted to act;
translations.idiomatic: Just as Shaocheng was about to go out to feast the imperial envoy, Chang, Ji, and others set their plot in motion;

sentences.zh: 臨發，為人所告，常、冀先遇害。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure he was reported by someone; Chang and Ji were killed first.
translations.idiomatic: Just as they were about to set out, someone informed on them; Chang and Ji were put to death first.

sentences.zh: 其將李嘉節等各持假詔請罪，少誠悉宥之。

translations.literal: His generals Li Jiajie and others each held forged edicts to plead guilt; Shaocheng pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: Generals such as Li Jiajie each presented forged edicts begging forgiveness; Shaocheng pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 其大將宋炅、曹齊奔歸京師。

translations.literal: His great generals Song Jiong and Cao Qi fled back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His chief generals Song Jiong and Cao Qi fled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十五年，陳許節度曲環卒，少誠擅出兵攻掠臨潁縣，節度留後上官涚遣兵赴救，臨潁鎮使韋清與少誠通，救兵三千余人，悉擒縛而去。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Qu Huan, military governor of Chenxu, died; Shaocheng on his own authority sent troops to attack and plunder Linying County. Acting military governor Shangguan Hui dispatched troops to the rescue. Linying garrison commander Wei Qing was in league with Shaocheng; more than three thousand relief troops were all captured and bound and taken away.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Chenxu military governor Qu Huan died. Shaocheng unauthorizedly sent troops to raid Linying. Acting governor Shangguan Hui sent relief, but garrison commander Wei Qing colluded with Shaocheng; all three thousand-odd rescuers were seized and carried off.

sentences.zh: 九月，遂圍許州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he then besieged Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he laid siege to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋下詔削奪少誠官爵，分遣十六道兵馬進討。

translations.literal: Soon an edict was issued stripping Shaocheng of rank and titles, and troops from sixteen circuits were dispatched in separate columns to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the throne stripped Shaocheng of office and enfeoffment and sent armies from sixteen circuits against him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，官軍敗衄於小溵河。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the imperial army was routed at the Small Yin River.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month government forces were defeated at the Small Yin River.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，夏州節度使韓全義為淮蔡招討處置使，北路行營諸軍將士，並取全義指揮，陳許節度留後上官涚充副使。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year Han Quanyi, military governor of Xia Prefecture, was made Pacification and Disposition Commissioner for Huai-Cai; all generals and soldiers of the northern-route field army were placed under Quanyi's command, and Chenxu acting military governor Shangguan Hui was made deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The next first month Xia military governor Han Quanyi became Huai-Cai pacification commissioner; northern-route forces answered to him, with Shangguan Hui as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 五月，全義與少誠將吳秀、吳少陽等戰於溵水南，官軍復敗。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Quanyi fought with Shaocheng's generals Wu Xiu, Wu Shaoyang, and others at the south bank of the Yin River, and the government army was again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In fifth month Han Quanyi fought Wu Shaocheng's generals Wu Xiu and Wu Shaoyang at the south bank of the Yin River, and imperial troops were defeated again.

sentences.zh: 七月，全義頓軍於五樓行營，為賊所乘，大潰，全義與都監軍使賈秀英、賈國良等夜遁，遂城守溵水。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Quanyi halted his army at the Wulou encampment; the rebels seized the opportunity and he was thoroughly routed; Quanyi with Army Supervisory Commissioner Jia Xiuying, Jia Guoliang, and others fled by night, and then fortified and held Yinshui.
translations.idiomatic: In seventh month Han Quanyi encamped at Wulou; the rebels struck and his army collapsed. Quanyi fled by night with supervisors Jia Xiuying and Jia Guoliang and fell back to fortify Yinshui.

sentences.zh: 汴宋、徐泗、淄青兵馬直趣陳州，列營四面。

translations.literal: The Bian-Song, Xu-Si, and Zi-Qing armies and horses went straight to Chen Prefecture and encamped on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Armies from Bian-Song, Xu-Si, and Zi-Qing marched straight to Chenzhou and encircled it.

sentences.zh: 少誠兵逼溵水五、六里下營，韓全義諸軍又退保陳州。

translations.literal: Shaocheng's troops pressed to within five or six li of Yinshui and made camp; Han Quanyi's various armies again withdrew to defend Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shaocheng camped within five or six li of Yinshui, and Han Quanyi's forces withdrew again to Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 其汴州、河陽等兵各私歸本道，陳許將孟元陽與神策兵各率所部留軍溵水。

translations.literal: The Bian Prefecture, Heyang, and other troops each privately returned to their home circuits; Chen-Xu general Meng Yuanyang and the Shence troops each led their own sections to remain and garrison Yinshui.
translations.idiomatic: Troops from Bianzhou, Heyang, and other commands drifted home, while Meng Yuanyang of Chen-Xu and the Shence army remained at Yinshui.

sentences.zh: 全義斬昭義、滑州、河陽、河中都將凡四人，然竟未嘗整陣交鋒，而王師累挫潰。

translations.literal: Quanyi beheaded four generals of Zhaoyi, Hua Prefecture, Heyang, and Hezhong in all; yet in the end he never once formed ranks and crossed blades, while the imperial army repeatedly suffered defeat and rout.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi executed four generals from Zhaoyi, Hua, Heyang, and Hezhong, yet never fought a pitched battle while imperial armies kept breaking.

sentences.zh: 少誠尋引兵退歸蔡州。

translations.literal: Shaocheng soon led his troops back to Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shaocheng soon withdrew to Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 遂下詔洗雪，復其官爵，累加檢校僕射。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict cleared and restored him, reinstating his office and rank, and repeatedly added the honorary post of Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The court then issued a reconciling edict, restored his titles, and repeatedly promoted him to honorary vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，加同中書門平章事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shunzong acceded, he was added as Co-Regulator of the Department of State Affairs and the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong succeeded, Wu Shaocheng was made co-regulator of the Department of State Affairs and the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 元和初，遷檢校司空，依前平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, he was transferred to Honorary Minister of Works, continuing as before in the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yuanhe he was promoted to honorary minister of works while retaining his chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 元和四年十一月卒，年六十，廢朝三日，贈司徒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Yuanhe he died, aged sixty; court audience was suspended for three days, and he was posthumously awarded Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He died in eleventh month, Yuanhe 4, at sixty; court mourned for three days and posthumously made him minister of education.

sentences.zh: 吳少陽，本滄州清池人。

translations.literal: Wu Shaoyang was originally a native of Qingchi in Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shaoyang was originally from Qingchi in Cang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，吳少誠父翔在魏博軍中，與少陽相愛。

translations.literal: At first, when Wu Shaocheng's father Xiang was in the Weibo army, he and Shaoyang were fond of each other.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, Wu Shaocheng's father Xiang served in the Weibo army and was close to Shaoyang.

sentences.zh: 及少誠知淮西留守，乃厚以金帛取少陽至，則名以堂弟，署為軍職，累奏官爵，出入少誠家，情旨甚暱。

translations.literal: When Shaocheng became acting governor of Huaixi he richly rewarded Shaoyang with gold and silks to bring him there, then styled him a younger cousin by the hall, appointed him to a military post, repeatedly memorialized for his titles, and had him enter and leave Shaocheng's household; their intimacy was very close.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shaocheng held Huaixi, he lavished gold and silks to summon Shaoyang, named him a hall cousin, gave him military office, repeatedly sought court titles for him, and kept him in and out of his house in the closest trust.

sentences.zh: 少陽度少誠猜忍，懼為所害，乃請出外以任防捍之任，少誠乃表為申州刺史、兼御史大夫，凡五年。

translations.literal: Shaoyang judged Shaocheng suspicious and cruel, feared being harmed by him, and therefore asked to go outside to take charge of frontier defense; Shaocheng then memorialized him as prefect of Shen and concurrent Grand Censor, for five years in all.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Shaocheng's cruelty, Shaoyang asked for an outside post on frontier defense; Shaocheng had him made Shen prefect and Grand Censor for five years.

sentences.zh: 少陽頗寬易，而少誠之眾悅附焉。

translations.literal: Shaoyang was rather easygoing, and Shaocheng's troops were glad to attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyang was comparatively mild, and Shaocheng's soldiers gladly rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 及少誠病亟，家僮單於熊兒者，偽以少誠意取少陽至，時少誠已不知人，乃偽署少陽攝副使、知軍州事。

translations.literal: When Shaocheng fell gravely ill, a household slave named Shan Yu Xiong'er falsely used Shaocheng's intent to summon Shaoyang; by then Shaocheng no longer knew men, and he falsely appointed Shaoyang acting deputy commissioner and controller of military and prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As Shaocheng lay dying, the slave Shan Yu Xiong'er forged his master's will to fetch Shaoyang; Shaocheng was already insensible, and the slave falsely named Shaoyang acting deputy and governor of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 少誠子元慶，年二十余，先為軍職，兼御史中丞，少陽密害之。

translations.literal: Shaocheng's son Yuanqing, a little over twenty, had earlier held a military post and was also Vice Censor-in-chief; Shaoyang secretly killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shaocheng's son Yuanqing, in his twenties and already a military officer and Vice Censor-in-chief, was secretly killed by Shaoyang.

sentences.zh: 及少誠死，少陽自為留後。

translations.literal: When Shaocheng died, Shaoyang made himself acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: After Shaocheng's death Shaoyang declared himself acting governor.

sentences.zh: 時王承宗求繼士真，不受詔；

translations.literal: At that time Wang Chengzong sought to succeed Shi Zhen and would not accept the edict;
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wang Chengzong sought to inherit Shi Zhen's post and defied the throne;

sentences.zh: 憲宗怒，以討承宗，不欲兵連兩河，乃詔遂王宥遙領彰義軍節度大使，以少陽為留後。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and was campaigning against Chengzong; not wishing troops to engage both Hebei circuits, he ordered Prince Su Wang You to hold the Zhangyi commandery in absentia and made Shaoyang acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong, angry and attacking Chengzong, did not want war on two Hebei fronts; he had Prince Su Wang You hold Zhangyi in name and confirmed Shaoyang as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 遂授彰義軍節度使、檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was then appointed military governor of Zhangyi and Inspector of the Ministry of Works on probation.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyang was then made Zhangyi military governor and provisional Inspector of Works.

sentences.zh: 少陽據蔡州凡五年，不朝覲。

translations.literal: Shaoyang held Cai Prefecture for five years in all and never came to court.
translations.idiomatic: For five years Shaoyang held Cai and never presented himself at court.

sentences.zh: 汝南多廣野大澤，得豢馬畜，時奪掠壽州茶山之利，內則數匿亡命，以富實其軍。

translations.literal: South of the Ru had broad marshes and great swamps suitable for raising horses and livestock; from time to time he seized the profits of Shou Prefecture's tea mountains, and within his borders he repeatedly harbored fugitives to enrich his army.
translations.idiomatic: The Ru region's open marshes fed his herds; he repeatedly raided Shou's tea revenues, harbored fugitives within his borders, and used both to fill his ranks.

sentences.zh: 又屢以牧馬來獻，詔因善之。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly presented tribute horses to pasture, and by edict the court therefore treated him favorably.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent horses as tribute more than once, and the court grew kindly disposed toward him.

sentences.zh: 元和九年九月卒，贈右僕射。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the ninth year of Yuanhe he died and was posthumously given Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of Yuanhe 9 and was posthumously made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 吳元濟，少陽長子也。

translations.literal: Wu Yuanji was Shaoyang's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuanji was Shaoyang's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 初為試協律郎、兼監察御史、攝蔡州刺史。

translations.literal: He had first served as Trial Coordinator of Music, concurrent Supervising Censor, and acting prefect of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: He had first been Trial Coordinator of Music, concurrent Supervising Censor, and acting Cai prefect.

sentences.zh: 及父死，不發喪，以病聞，因假為少陽表，請元濟主兵務。

translations.literal: When his father died he did not announce the mourning but reported illness, and on that pretext forged a memorial in Shaoyang's name asking that Yuanji take charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On his father's death he concealed the mourning, reported illness, and forged a memorial in Shaoyang's name asking that he command the army.

sentences.zh: 帝遣醫工候之，即稱少陽疾愈，不見而還。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a court physician to examine him; he at once claimed Shaoyang's illness was cured, would not receive him, and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a physician; Yuanji declared Shaoyang recovered, refused to receive him, and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 先是，少陽判官蘇兆、楊元卿及其將侯惟清嘗同為少陽畫朝覲計；

translations.literal: Earlier, Shaoyang's administrative aides Su Zhao and Yang Yuanqing and his general Hou Weiqing had together drawn up a plan for Shaoyang to attend court;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shaoyang's aides Su Zhao and Yang Yuanqing and his general Hou Weiqing had together planned his audience at court;

sentences.zh: 及元濟自領軍，兇狠無義，唯暱軍中兇悍之徒。

translations.literal: When Yuanji took command of the army himself he was fierce and ruthless without righteousness and trusted only the most violent men in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuanji seized the army he was savage and faithless and kept only the fiercest soldiers near him.

sentences.zh: 素不便兆，縊殺之，歸其屍於家，械侯惟清而囚之。

translations.literal: He had long disliked Zhao; he strangled him and returned the corpse to his family, and shackled Hou Weiqing and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He had long hated Zhao, strangled him and sent the body home, and chained Hou Weiqing in prison.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷誤聞惟清已死，贈兵部尚書，贈蘇兆以右僕射。

translations.literal: At the time the court mistakenly heard that Weiqing was already dead and posthumously made him Minister of War; Zhao was posthumously made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: The court wrongly heard Weiqing was dead and posthumously made him Minister of War; Zhao was posthumously made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 楊元卿先奏事在京師，得盡言經略淮西事於宰相李吉甫。

translations.literal: Yang Yuanqing had earlier gone to court to report and was able to tell Chief Councilor Li Jiyuan everything about strategy against Huaixi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuanqing had already gone to the capital and told Chief Councilor Li Jiyuan the full plan for Huaixi.

sentences.zh: 始，少陽以病聞，元卿請凡淮西使在道路者，所在留止之。

translations.literal: At first, when Shaoyang reported illness, Yuanqing asked that every Huaixi envoy on the road be detained wherever found.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyang first reported illness, Yuanqing asked that every Huaixi envoy on the roads be held wherever found.

sentences.zh: 及少陽卒，凡四十日，不為輟朝，但易將加兵於外以待。

translations.literal: When Shaoyang died, for forty days in all court was not suspended; they only replaced generals and added troops outside to wait.
translations.idiomatic: After Shaoyang's death court went on for forty days without mourning; they only rotated generals and massed troops outside to wait.

sentences.zh: 其邸吏無何妄傳董重質已殺元濟，並屠其家；

translations.literal: A clerk in the Huaixi residence rashly reported that Dong Chongzhi had already killed Yuanji and slaughtered his family;
translations.idiomatic: A clerk at the Huaixi lodge falsely reported that Dong Chongzhi had killed Yuanji and exterminated his household;

sentences.zh: 李吉甫遽請對拜賀，乃輟朝。

translations.literal: Li Jiyuan hurried to ask for an audience to offer congratulations, and only then was court suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiyuan rushed to congratulate the emperor, and only then was court suspended.

sentences.zh: 數日，知元濟尚在。

translations.literal: Several days later they learned Yuanji was still alive.
translations.idiomatic: Days later they learned Yuanji still lived.

sentences.zh: 時賊陰計已成，群眾四出，狂悍而不可遏，屠舞陽，焚葉縣，攻掠魯山、襄城。

translations.literal: By then the rebels' secret plans were complete; the masses poured out in all directions, wild and fierce and impossible to restrain; they slaughtered Wuyang, burned Ye County, and attacked and plundered Lushan and Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels' plot was ripe; bands ranged abroad, savage and unstoppable—slaughtering Wuyang, burning Ye, raiding Lushan and Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 汝州、許州及陽翟人多逃伏山谷荊棘間，為其殺傷驅剽者千里，關東大恐。

translations.literal: People of Ruzhou, Xuzhou, and Yangdi mostly fled and hid in mountain valleys and brambles; those killed, wounded, driven, and plundered by them extended a thousand li; east of the passes there was great terror.
translations.idiomatic: People of Ru, Xu, and Yangdi fled into hills and thickets; killing and plunder reached a thousand li; the eastern provinces were terrified.

sentences.zh: 十月，以陳州刺史李光顏為忠武軍節度使，又以山南東道節度使嚴綬充申光蔡等州招撫使，仍令內常侍崔潭峻監綬軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Li Guangyan, prefect of Chen, was made military governor of Zhongwu; Yan Shou, military governor of Shannan East, was made pacification commissioner for Shen, Guang, Cai, and other prefectures, and Palace Attendant Cui Tanjun was ordered to supervise Shou's army.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Chen prefect Li Guangyan became Zhongwu military governor; Shannan East governor Yan Shou became pacification commissioner for Shen, Guang, Cai, and related prefectures, with Palace Attendant Cui Tanjun to oversee his army.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，綬軍臨賊西境。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year Shou's army reached the rebels' western border.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, first month, Shou's army reached the western edge of rebel territory.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict said:
translations.idiomatic: The edict read:

sentences.zh: 吳元濟逆絕人理，反易天常；

translations.literal: Wu Yuanji has rebelled against human principle and overturned Heaven's constant order;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuanji has defied all human order and overturned Heaven's law;

sentences.zh: 不居父喪，擅領軍政。

translations.literal: he does not observe mourning for his father and on his own authority holds military and civil power.
translations.idiomatic: he refuses his father's mourning and seizes military and civil authority.

sentences.zh: 諭以詔旨，曾無謙恭，熒惑一方之人，迫脅三軍之眾。

translations.literal: When instructed by imperial edict he showed no humility; he deludes the people of a region and coerces the masses of three armies.
translations.idiomatic: Told by edict, he showed no deference; he misleads a province and coerces three armies.

sentences.zh: 以少陽嘗經任使，為之軫悼，命申吊祭，臨遣使臣。

translations.literal: Because Shaoyang was once employed by the throne, We were moved to grief for him and ordered condolences and libations and the dispatch of envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shaoyang once served Us, We mourned him, ordered rites of condolence, and sent envoys.

sentences.zh: 陵虐封疆，遂致稽阻，絕朝廷之理，忘父子之恩。

translations.literal: He tyrannized the borders and thereby caused obstruction; he cut off the court's authority and forgot the kindness between father and son.
translations.idiomatic: He ravaged the frontier and blocked Our messengers, severing loyalty to the throne and trampling the bond between father and son.

sentences.zh: 旋又掩寇舞陽，傷殘吏卒，焚燒葉縣，騷擾閭閻，恣行奪攘，無所畏忌。

translations.literal: Then again he raided Wuyang, wounded officials and soldiers, burned Ye County, disturbed villages and lanes, and plundered at will without fear.
translations.idiomatic: Then he raided Wuyang, maimed officers and soldiers, burned Ye, terrorized the countryside, and plundered without restraint.

sentences.zh: 朕念賞延之義，重傷籓帥之門，尚欲納於忠順之途，處在顯榮之地。

translations.literal: We recall the meaning of rewarding the good and deeply grieve for a frontier house; We still wished to place him on the path of loyalty and in a place of honor.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of reward for loyalty and grieving for a frontier clan, We still wished to set him on the path of obedience and honor.

sentences.zh: 未能飭怒，猶為包荒，再降詔書，俾申招撫。

translations.literal: Unable to restrain Our anger, We still covered his excesses; We lowered edicts again to extend pacification.
translations.idiomatic: We could not yet unleash Our wrath and still indulged his crimes, lowering edicts again to offer reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 而毒螫滋甚，奸心靡悛，壽春西南，又陷鎮柵，窮兇稔惡，縱暴延災。

translations.literal: Yet his poison grew worse and his treacherous heart would not repent; southwest of Shouchun he again seized fortified posts; his evil ripened and his violence spread disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his venom deepened and his treachery would not turn; southwest of Shouchun he seized more forts—evil ripe, violence spreading.

sentences.zh: 覆載之所不容，人神之所共棄，良非獲已，致此興戎。

translations.literal: What Heaven and Earth cannot bear, what gods and men together cast away—truly not obtained willingly did We bring forth this campaign.
translations.idiomatic: What Heaven and Earth cannot tolerate, what gods and men alike reject—not lightly did We raise arms.

sentences.zh: 吳元濟在身官爵，並宜令削奪。

translations.literal: Wu Yuanji's offices and titles in his person are all to be stripped.
translations.idiomatic: All offices and titles held by Wu Yuanji in his person are revoked.

sentences.zh: 令宣武、大寧、淮南、宣歙等道兵馬合勢，山南東道及魏博、荊南、江西、劍南東川兵馬與鄂嶽許會，東都防禦使與懷鄭汝節度及義成兵馬掎角相應，同期進討。

translations.literal: Order the Xuanwu, Daning, Huainan, Xuan-She, and other circuits to combine their forces; Shannan East and the armies of Weibo, Jingnan, Jiangxi, and Sword River East Sichuan to join E-Yue at the rendezvous; the Eastern Capital defense commissioner with Huai, Zheng, Ru military governors and Yicheng troops to coordinate in pincer fashion and advance together on the same schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Let Xuanwu, Daning, Huainan, Xuan-She, and other circuits unite; Shannan East with Weibo, Jingnan, Jiangxi, and East Sichuan join E-Yue; the Luoyang defender with Huai, Zheng, and Ru governors and Yicheng troops pinch from another angle—all to attack on one timetable.

sentences.zh: 二月，綬兵為賊所襲，敗於磁丘，退保唐州。

translations.literal: In the second month Shou's troops were attacked by the rebels and defeated at Ciqu, retreating to defend Tang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Shou was ambushed and beaten at Ciqu, withdrawing to Tang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四月，光顏破賊黨，元濟遣人求援於鎮州王承宗、淄鄆李師道；

translations.literal: In the fourth month Guangyan broke the rebel band; Yuanji sent men to ask aid of Zhenzhou's Wang Chengzong and Zi-Yan's Li Shidao;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Guangyan routed the rebels; Yuanji sought help from Wang Chengzong of Zhen and Li Shidao of Zi-Yan;

sentences.zh: 二帥上表於朝廷，請赦元濟之罪，朝旨不從。

translations.literal: the two frontier lords memorialized the court asking pardon for Yuanji's crime; the court's intent did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: both lords memorialized for Yuanji's pardon; the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 自是兩河賊帥所在竊發，冀以沮撓王師。

translations.literal: From this the rebel leaders of the two Hebei circuits everywhere stirred up trouble in secret, hoping to thwart the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Hebei warlords stirred trouble wherever they could to obstruct the imperial campaign.

sentences.zh: 五月，承宗、師道遣盜燒河陰倉，詔御史中丞裴度於軍前宣喻，觀用兵形勢。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Chengzong and Shidao sent thieves to burn the Heyin granary; Censor-in-chief Pei Du was ordered to announce the imperial will at the front and observe the shape of the war.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Chengzong and Shidao sent agents to burn the Heyin granaries; Censor-in-chief Pei Du was sent to the front to proclaim the throne's will and survey the war.

sentences.zh: 度還奏曰：「臣觀諸將，唯光顏勇義盡心，必有成功。」

translations.literal: Du returned and memorialized, saying: "Your servant has observed the generals; only Guangyan is brave and loyal with all his heart—he will surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Du reported: "Of all the generals, only Guangyan serves with full courage and loyalty; he will prevail."

sentences.zh: 上意甚悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 翌日，光顏奏大破賊於時曲，上曰：「度知光顏，可謂至矣！」

translations.literal: The next day Guangyan reported a great defeat of the rebels at Shiqu; the emperor said: "Du knows Guangyan—one may call that perfect knowledge!
translations.idiomatic: Next day Guangyan reported a great victory at Shiqu; the emperor said, "Du knows Guangyan to the marrow!"

sentences.zh: 乃以度兼刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He then made Du concurrent Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He then made Du concurrent Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 自是中外相賀，決不赦賊，征天下兵環申、蔡之郊，大小十余鎮。

translations.literal: From this inside and outside congratulated one another and resolved never to pardon the rebels; troops from all the empire ringed the borders of Shen and Cai, more than ten large commands in all.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country rejoiced and vowed no pardon; armies from across the realm encircled Shen and Cai in more than ten major camps.

sentences.zh: 六月，承宗、師道遣盜伏於京城，殺宰相武元衡、中丞裴度；

translations.literal: In the sixth month Chengzong and Shidao sent thieves lying in wait in the capital and killed Chief Councilor Wu Yuanheng and Censor-in-chief Pei Du;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Chengzong and Shidao sent assassins to the capital, killing Chief Councilor Wu Yuanheng and wounding Censor-in-chief Pei Du;

sentences.zh: 衡先死，度重傷而免。

translations.literal: Yuanheng died first; Du was severely wounded but escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng died; Du was gravely wounded but survived.

sentences.zh: 憲宗特怒，即命度為宰相，淮右用兵之事，一以委之。

translations.literal: Xianzong was especially enraged and at once appointed Du chief councilor; affairs of the Huaiyou campaign were wholly entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong's wrath was fierce; he made Du chief councilor and entrusted the entire Huaiyou war to him.

sentences.zh: 七月，李師道遣嵩山僧圓凈結山賊與留邸兵，欲焚燒東都，先事敗而禍弭。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Li Shidao sent the Song Mountain monk Yuanjing to join mountain bandits with troops left at the postal lodge, intending to burn the Eastern Capital; the affair was exposed first and the disaster was averted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Shidao sent the monk Yuanjing of Song Mountain to join bandits and lodge troops in a plot to burn Luoyang; the plot failed before harm was done.

sentences.zh: 嚴綬退罷，乃以汴州節度使韓弘為淮右行營兵馬都統；

translations.literal: Yan Shou was removed and demoted; then Bianzhou military governor Han Hong was made overall commander of Huaiyou field forces;
translations.idiomatic: Shou was dismissed; Bianzhou governor Han Hong became overall commander of the Huaiyou campaign;

sentences.zh: 以高霞寓有名，用為唐鄧節度。

translations.literal: Because Gao Xiayu had a reputation, he was used as Tang-Deng military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xiayu, famed for his record, was made Tang-Deng military governor.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，諸軍雲合，惟李光顏、懷汝節度烏重胤心無顧望，旦夕血戰，繼獻戎捷。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year the armies gathered like clouds; only Li Guangyan and Huai-Ru military governor Wu Zhongyin had no second thoughts and day and night fought bloody battles, repeatedly presenting martial trophies.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year's spring the hosts massed; only Guangyan and Huai-Ru governor Wu Zhongyin fought without hesitation, day and night, and sent victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 六月，高霞寓為賊所擊，敗於鐵城，退保新興柵。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Gao Xiayu was struck by the rebels and defeated at Iron City, retreating to defend the Xinxing stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Xiayu was beaten at Iron City and fell back to the Xinxing stockade.

sentences.zh: 時諸軍勝負皆不實聞，多虛稱克捷；

translations.literal: At the time victories and defeats of the various armies were not truthfully reported; many falsely claimed captures.
translations.idiomatic: Reports from the fronts were false; many commanders claimed victories they had not won.

sentences.zh: 及霞寓敗，中外恟々。

translations.literal: When Xiayu was defeated, inside and outside were alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiayu's defeat threw court and country into alarm.

sentences.zh: 宰相諫官屢以罷兵為請，唯裴度堅於破賊。

translations.literal: Censors and remonstrating officials repeatedly asked to stop the campaign; only Pei Du insisted on breaking the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Censors and remonstrators repeatedly begged to halt the war; only Pei Du held firm for victory.

sentences.zh: 尋以袁滋代霞寓為唐鄧帥，滋柔懦不能軍。

translations.literal: Soon Yuan Ci replaced Xiayu as Tang-Deng commander; Ci was gentle and weak and could not command an army.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ci replaced Xiayu at Tang-Deng; Ci was soft and could not lead troops.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，袁滋復貶，閑廄使李醖表請軍前自效，乃用醖為唐鄧帥以代滋。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year Yuan Ci was demoted again; Privy Purse envoy Li Su asked to offer himself at the front, and Su was used as Tang-Deng commander to replace Ci.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year's first month Ci was demoted again; Privy Purse envoy Li Su volunteered for the front and replaced him.

sentences.zh: 醖軍壓境，拔賊文城柵，擒柵將吳秀琳，又獲賊將李祐。

translations.literal: Su pressed the border, took the rebels' Wencheng stockade, captured stockade commander Wu Xiulin, and also took rebel general Li You.
translations.idiomatic: Su advanced, stormed Wencheng stockade, seized Wu Xiulin, and captured Li You.

sentences.zh: 李光顏亦拔賊郾城。

translations.literal: Li Guangyan also took the rebels' Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan also took Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 元濟始懼，盡發左右及守城卒，屬董重質以抗光顏、重胤。

translations.literal: Yuanji began to fear and sent out all his close attendants and garrison troops, putting Dong Chongzhi in charge to resist Guangyan and Zhongyin.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji grew afraid, stripped his garrison and household guard, and set Dong Chongzhi against Guangyan and Zhongyin.

sentences.zh: 六月，元濟乞降，為群賊所制，不能自拔。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Yuanji begged to surrender but was controlled by the rebel band and could not extricate himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Yuanji sought to surrender but the rebel chiefs held him fast.

sentences.zh: 上以元兇已蹙，兵未臨於賊城，輓饋日殫，因延英問計於宰相。

translations.literal: The emperor thought the chief culprit was already pressed and troops had not yet reached the rebel city; supply wagons were daily exhausted; he therefore questioned the chief councilors at the Yanching Hall on strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought Yuanji cornered yet the armies had not reached Cai and supplies ran thin; he asked his councilors at the Yanching Hall for counsel.

sentences.zh: 裴度曰：「賊力已困，但群帥不一，故未能決降。」

translations.literal: Pei Du said: "The rebels' strength is already exhausted; only because the frontier lords are not of one mind can they not yet decide to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du said, "The rebels are spent; only disunity among our generals keeps them from surrender."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿決能行乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Can you surely go?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Can you go yourself?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「臣誓不與賊偕全。」

translations.literal: He said: "Your servant vows not to survive with the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I swear not to return if the rebels stand."

sentences.zh: 七月，詔以度為彰義軍節度使，兼申光蔡四面行營招撫使，以郾城為行在，蔡州為節度所。

translations.literal: In the seventh month an edict made Du military governor of Zhangyi and concurrent pacification commissioner for the four sides of Shen, Guang, and Cai; Yancheng was made headquarters and Cai Prefecture the governorship seat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Du was made Zhangyi military governor and pacification commissioner for Shen, Guang, and Cai on all sides, with headquarters at Yancheng and the governorship at Cai.

sentences.zh: 八月，度至郾城，激勵士眾，軍士喜度至，以賞罰必行，皆願輸罄；

translations.literal: In the eighth month Du reached Yancheng, roused officers and soldiers; the troops rejoiced at Du's arrival because rewards and punishments would surely be enforced, and all wished to give their utmost;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Du reached Yancheng and stirred the ranks; the soldiers welcomed him, knowing discipline would be real, and offered their last strength;

sentences.zh: 每出勞，軍士有流涕者。

translations.literal: whenever he went out to comfort them some soldiers wept.
translations.idiomatic: when he went among them some wept.

sentences.zh: 時李醖營文城柵，既得吳秀琳、李祐，知其可用，委信無疑，日夜與計事於帳中。

translations.literal: At that time Li Su was encamped at Wencheng stockade; having obtained Wu Xiulin and Li You and knowing they could be used, he trusted them without doubt and day and night planned affairs with them in his tent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Su held Wencheng; trusting Xiulin and You after capturing them, he plotted with them nightly in his tent.

sentences.zh: 祐曰：「元濟勁軍，多在洄曲西境防捍，而守蔡者皆市人疲耄之卒，可以乘虛掩襲，直抵懸匏，比賊將聞之，元濟成擒矣！」

translations.literal: You said: "Yuanji's crack troops are mostly on the western border of Huaiqu on defense, while those guarding Cai are market men and worn-out old soldiers; one can take advantage of emptiness in a surprise raid straight to the Hanging Gourd—before the rebel generals hear of it Yuanji will be captured!
translations.idiomatic: You said, "Yuanji's best troops guard Huaiqu's west; Cai is held by shopkeepers and old men. Strike the gap, rush the Hanging Gourd, and Yuanji is ours before his generals know."

sentences.zh: 醖然之，咨於裴度。

translations.literal: Su approved and consulted Pei Du.
translations.idiomatic: Su agreed and consulted Pei Du.

sentences.zh: 度曰：「兵非出奇不勝，常侍良圖也。」

translations.literal: Du said: "In war nothing succeeds without the unexpected—Regular Attendant, your plan is excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Du said, "War demands surprise—your plan is sound."

sentences.zh: 十一月，醖夜出軍，令李祐率勁騎三千為前鋒，田進誠三千為後軍，醖自率三千為中軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Su marched out by night, ordering Li You to lead three thousand crack horsemen as vanguard, Tian Jincheng three thousand as rear, and Su himself three thousand in the center.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Su marched by night: Li You with three thousand elite cavalry in front, Tian Jincheng three thousand in the rear, Su three thousand in the center.

sentences.zh: 其月十日夜，至蔡州城下，坎墻而畢登，賊不之覺。

translations.literal: On the night of the tenth of that month they reached below Cai Prefecture's walls, dug through the rampart and all climbed up; the rebels did not perceive them.
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth night they reached Cai, tunneled the wall, and scaled it unseen.

sentences.zh: 十一日，攻衙城，擒元濟並其家屬以聞。

translations.literal: On the eleventh they attacked the yamen city, captured Yuanji and his household, and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh they stormed the administrative compound, seized Yuanji and his family, and sent word.

sentences.zh: 初，元濟之叛，恃其兇狠，然治軍無紀綱。

translations.literal: At first, when Yuanji rebelled, he relied on his fierceness, yet in governing the army there was no discipline.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanji rebelled he trusted his brutality, yet his army had no discipline.

sentences.zh: 其將趙昌洪、淩朝江、董重質等各權兵外寇。

translations.literal: His generals Zhao Changhong, Ling Chaojiang, Dong Chongzhi, and others each held troops and raided outside.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Zhao Changhong, Ling Chaojiang, Dong Chongzhi, and others each led armies abroad.

sentences.zh: 李師道鄆州之鹽，城往來寧陵、雍丘之間，韓弘知而不禁。

translations.literal: Li Shidao's Yanzhou salt went back and forth between Ningling and Yongqiu; Han Hong knew but did not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao's Yanzhou salt caravans moved between Ningling and Yongqiu; Han Hong knew and did not stop them.

sentences.zh: 淮右自少誠阻兵已來，三十余年，王師加討，未嘗及其城下，嘗走韓全義，敗於頔，故驕悍無所顧忌。

translations.literal: Since Huaiyou first blocked the army under Shaocheng, more than thirty years had passed; when the imperial army attacked they had never reached below the city walls; they had once routed Han Quanyi and been defeated at Yong, and therefore were arrogant and fierce without regard.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyou had defied the throne since Shaocheng—over thirty years. Imperial armies had never reached their walls; they had routed Han Quanyi and survived defeat at Yong, and so feared nothing.

sentences.zh: 且恃城池重固，有陂浸阻回，故以天下兵環攻三年，所克者一縣而已。

translations.literal: Moreover they relied on heavy, solid walls and moats and ponds blocking approach, so though armies of the empire besieged them for three years, they took only one county.
translations.idiomatic: They also relied on stout walls and flooded moats that blocked approach, so though imperial armies ringed them for three years, only one county was taken.

sentences.zh: 及黜高霞寓、李遜、袁滋，諸軍始進。

translations.literal: When Gao Xiayu, Li Xun, and Yuan Ci were removed, the various armies at last advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gao Xiayu, Li Xun, and Yuan Ci were dismissed, the allied armies at last advanced.

sentences.zh: 又得陰山府沙阤驍騎、邯鄲勇卒，光顏、重胤之奮命，及丞相臨統，破諸將首尾之計，力擒元惡。

translations.literal: They also obtained the fierce cavalry of the Yinshan garrison Shatuo, brave troops of Handan, Guangyan and Zhongyin fighting desperately, and the chancellor commanding in person, breaking the generals' plan to hold back at both ends, and capturing the chief villain by force.
translations.idiomatic: They also had the fierce Shatuo cavalry of the Yinshan garrison, brave Handan troops, Guangyan and Zhongyin fighting desperately, and the chancellor commanding in person—breaking the generals' strategy of holding back at both ends and capturing the chief villain by force.

sentences.zh: 申、蔡之始，人劫於希烈、少誠之虐法，而忘其所歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shen and Cai, people were coerced by the cruel laws of Xilie and Shaocheng and forgot where they belonged.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning at Shen and Cai, people were coerced by the cruel laws of Xilie and Shaocheng and forgot their allegiance.

sentences.zh: 數十年之後，長者衰喪，而壯者安於毒暴而恬於搏噬。

translations.literal: After several decades the elders had passed away, and the young grew accustomed to poison and violence and took killing for granted.
translations.idiomatic: After several decades the elders had died off, and the young grew accustomed to cruelty and violence and took slaughter for granted.

sentences.zh: 地既少馬，而廣畜騾，乘之教戰，謂之騾子軍。

translations.literal: The land had few horses but raised mules widely; they were trained for war and called the Mule Army.
translations.idiomatic: The region had few horses but raised many mules, trained them for war, and called them the Mule Army.

sentences.zh: 尤稱勇悍，而甲仗皆畫為雷公星文，以為厭勝；

translations.literal: They were especially famed for fierce courage, and their armor was all painted with Thunder Lord and star patterns as talismans;
translations.idiomatic: They were especially famed for ferocity, and their arms were painted with Thunder Lord and star patterns as charms against evil;

sentences.zh: 而少誠能以奸謀固眾心。

translations.literal: and Shaocheng could use cunning schemes to bind the troops' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: and Shaocheng could use cunning to bind the troops' loyalty.

sentences.zh: 初，韓全義敗於溵水，蔡兵於全義帳中得公卿間問訊書，少誠束而諭眾曰：「朝廷公卿以此書托全義，收蔡州日，乞一將士妻女以為婢妄。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Han Quanyi was defeated at Yinshui, Cai troops found among Quanyi's baggage letters of inquiry exchanged among the chief ministers; Shaocheng bound them and announced to the masses: "The court's chief ministers entrusted these letters to Quanyi—on the day Cai Prefecture is taken, each is to be given one soldier's wife or daughter as a servant girl.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Han Quanyi was defeated at Yinshui, Cai troops found in his baggage letters exchanged among chief ministers. Shaocheng bound them up and told the troops, "The court's ministers entrusted these to Quanyi—when Cai Prefecture falls, each is to receive a soldier's wife or daughter as a servant."

sentences.zh: 以此激怒其眾，絕其歸向之心。

translations.literal: With this he enraged his masses and cut off their wish to return.
translations.idiomatic: With this he enraged them and cut off any wish to submit.

sentences.zh: 是以蔡人有老死不聞天子恩宥者，故堅為賊用。

translations.literal: Thus there were people of Cai who lived to old age without ever hearing the Son of Heaven's grace, and so they steadfastly served the rebels.
