translations.idiomatic: Thus many in Cai lived to old age without ever hearing the emperor's mercy, and so they steadfastly served the rebels.

sentences.zh: 地雖中州，人心過於夷貊，乃至搜閱天下豪銳，三年而後屈者，彼非將才而力備，蓋勢驅性習，不知教義之所致也。

translations.literal: Though the land was in the central plain, hearts exceeded those of barbarians; when the empire searched out its finest fighters and only after three years prevailed, it was not because their generals were talented and their strength complete—rather custom driven by circumstance, ignorant of righteousness, was the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Though the land lay in the central plain, hearts were more savage than barbarians'. When the empire mustered its finest fighters and only after three years prevailed, it was not superior generalship but force of custom—ignorance of righteousness—that made it so hard.

sentences.zh: 元濟至京，憲宗禦興安門受浮，百僚樓前稱賀，乃獻廟社，徇於兩京，斬之於獨柳，時年三十五。

translations.literal: When Yuanji reached the capital, Xianzong received the captive at Xing'an Gate; the hundred officials congratulated him before the tower; he was presented to the ancestral temple and paraded through the two capitals, then beheaded at Duli; he was then thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanji reached the capital, Emperor Xianzong received the captive at Xing'an Gate. Officials congratulated from the tower; he was presented to the ancestral temple, paraded through both capitals, and beheaded at Duli at the age of thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 其夜失其首。

translations.literal: That night his head was lost.
translations.idiomatic: That night his head was stolen.

sentences.zh: 妻沈氏，沒入掖庭；

translations.literal: His wife Lady Shen was sent to the palace women's quarters;
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Shen was consigned to the palace women's quarters;

sentences.zh: 弟二人、子三人，流於江陵誅之；

translations.literal: two younger brothers and three sons were banished to Jiangling and executed;
translations.idiomatic: two younger brothers and three sons were banished to Jiangling and executed;

sentences.zh: 判官劉協庶七人皆斬。

translations.literal: Administrative Aide Liu Xieshu and seven others were all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Administrative Aide Liu Xieshu and seven others were all beheaded.

sentences.zh: 光、蔡等州平，始復為王土矣。

translations.literal: Guang, Cai, and other prefectures were pacified and at last returned to imperial soil.
translations.idiomatic: Guang, Cai, and other prefectures were pacified and at last returned to the throne's domain.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：治亂，勢也，勢亂不能卒治。

translations.literal: The historian says: Order and disorder are a matter of momentum; when momentum is chaotic it cannot be quickly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Order and disorder follow momentum; when momentum is chaotic, order cannot come quickly.

sentences.zh: 長源以法繩驕軍，禍不旋踵；

translations.literal: Changyuan restrained the arrogant army with law, and disaster followed without delay;
translations.idiomatic: Changyuan tried to restrain the arrogant army with law, and disaster followed swiftly;

sentences.zh: 則董公之寬柔不無謂。

translations.literal: thus Commissioner Dong's lenience was not without reason.
translations.idiomatic: thus Commissioner Dong's lenience was not without point.

sentences.zh: 古之名將，以陰謀怨望，鮮全其族者。

translations.literal: Ancient famed generals who harbored secret resentment rarely preserved their clans whole.
translations.idiomatic: Famed generals of old who harbored secret resentment rarely saw their clans survive intact.

sentences.zh: 董秦始奮忠義，多長者言，宜其顯赫，及失意挾邪，俄被淮陰之戮，惜哉！

translations.literal: Dong Qin at first exerted loyalty and righteousness and spoke much as an elder should; he deserved his eminence, yet when frustrated he embraced wickedness and soon suffered execution like Han Xin—pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: Dong Qin at first showed loyalty and spoke as an elder should; he deserved his eminence, yet when frustrated he turned wicked and soon suffered execution like Han Xin—a pity!

sentences.zh: 吳少誠為希烈之亂胎，雖謀奪其軍，及嗣而滅。

translations.literal: Wu Shaocheng was the seed of Xilie's disorder; though he plotted to seize his army, when he succeeded he was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shaocheng was the seed of Xilie's rebellion; though he seized command, his line was destroyed in the next generation.

sentences.zh: 而元濟效希烈之狂悖，謂無天地，人之兇險，一至於斯！

translations.literal: Yuanji imitated Xilie's mad defiance, acting as if heaven and earth did not exist—the viciousness of men can reach this extreme!
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji imitated Xilie's mad defiance, as if heaven and earth did not exist—human viciousness can go no further!

sentences.zh: 是知王者禦治之道，其可忽諸！

translations.literal: Thus one knows that a sovereign's way of governing cannot be neglected!
translations.idiomatic: This shows that a sovereign's art of rule cannot be neglected!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：聖哲之君，慎名與器。

translations.literal: Praise says: A sage ruler is careful with titles and regalia.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: A sage ruler is careful with names and instruments of authority.

sentences.zh: 不軌之臣，得寵則戾。

translations.literal: A disloyal minister, once favored, turns violent.
translations.idiomatic: A disloyal minister, once favored, turns violent.

sentences.zh: 董怨而族，吳悖而菹。

translations.literal: Dong resented and his clan was destroyed; Wu rebelled and was minced.
translations.idiomatic: Dong resented and his clan was destroyed; Wu rebelled and was torn apart.

sentences.zh: 好亂樂禍，可監前車。

translations.literal: Those who delight in chaos and rejoice in disaster may take warning from the cart ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Those who delight in chaos and rejoice in disaster should take warning from the overturned cart ahead.
